items.title: The one-body reduction trace law of the finite-mode permutation sectors
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a
complex Hilbert space of finite dimension $d\ge1$
([[def-hilbert-space]]), let $n\ge1$, let $H^{\otimes n}$ be the $n$-fold
completed tensor power with $H^{\otimes0}:=\mathbb C$, $H^{\otimes1}:=H$ and
$H^{\otimes(k+1)}:=H^{\otimes k}\widehat\otimes H$, let $(U_\pi)_{\pi\in S_n}$
be the permutation unitaries and let
$P_\sigma^{(n)}$, $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$, be the sector projections
([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]), with sector space
$$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(n)}\subseteq H^{\otimes n}.$$
For $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
be the operator of clause (a) below, and put
$$\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^n O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n}).$$
Identify $H^{\otimes n}$ with $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$ by the
surjective linear isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) below, and let
$\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}$ be the partial trace of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clause (a) over the
second factor of that identification. Then:

(a) *slot operators*: for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ and every
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ there is a unique $O^{(i)}\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$
with $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{i-1}\otimes Ov_i\otimes v_{i+1}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$
for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$; it satisfies $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$ and
$(O^*)^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$; in particular $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$;

(b) *parenthesisation*: the assignment
$v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$
extends to a surjective linear isometry
$J_n:H^{\otimes n}\to H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$; for $n=1$ the
empty product is $1\in\mathbb C$ and $J_1u=u\otimes1$;

(c) *permutation invariance*: $U_\pi\,\Sigma(O)\,U_\pi^*=\Sigma(O)$ for every
$\pi\in S_n$; consequently $\Sigma(O)$ preserves both sector spaces and commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$:
$$\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)};$$

(d) *trace law*: for every density operator $\rho$ on the sector space
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]]
clause (a)), let $j:\mathfrak H_n^\sigma\hookrightarrow H^{\otimes n}$ be
the isometric inclusion and define its zero extension
$\widetilde\rho:=j\rho j^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; then
for every $O\in\mathcal B(H)$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\,\operatorname{tr}(\gamma\,O)$,
where $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\bigl(J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}\bigr)\in\mathcal B(H)$;

(e) *the reduced operator is a density operator*: the operator $\gamma$ of
clause (d) is a density operator on $H$; it is independent of the choice of
slot in the sense that it equals the partial trace of $\widetilde\rho$ over
the other $n-1$ slots in the parenthesisation in which the retained slot is
the one the display names; for $n=1$, $\gamma=\rho$. If
$\mathfrak H_n^\sigma=\{0\}$, there is no density operator of trace one on
that sector, so clauses (d)-(e) make no assertion about a sector preparation;

(f) *scope*: clauses (a)-(e) are exact operator identities on the
finite-dimensional labelled tensor powers; no physical system, particle
species, preparation or measurement is asserted, and the parameter $n$ is a
dimension count of the construction, not an observed particle number.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $H$ of dimension $d\ge1$, the integer $n\ge1$, the completed tensor powers $H^{\otimes n}$ with permutation unitaries $U_\pi$ and sector projections $P_\sigma^{(n)}$, the operator $O\in\mathcal B(H)$, the slot index $i$, and the density operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ with its zero extension $\widetilde\rho$.

[F1] **Tensor powers.** $H^{\otimes n}$ is a complex Hilbert space; the elementary tensors have dense linear span; $\|v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n\|=\|v_1\|\cdots\|v_n\|$ and $\langle v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle=\prod_{k}\langle v_k,w_k\rangle$; for orthonormal families spanning $H$ the corresponding elementary tensors form an orthonormal family with dense span ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] clauses (b), (c), (d)).

[F2] **Parenthesisation.** For every parenthesisation the iterated tensor product represents multilinear maps, and different parenthesisations are connected by the unique isomorphism preserving pure tensors ([[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]).

[F3] **Bounded tensor maps.** For complex Hilbert spaces $V,W$ and $S\in\mathcal B(V)$, $T\in\mathcal B(W)$ there is a unique $S\otimes T\in\mathcal B(V\widehat\otimes W)$ with $(S\otimes T)(u\otimes v)=Su\otimes Tv$, $\|S\otimes T\|\le\|S\|\,\|T\|$, $(S\otimes T)^*=S^*\otimes T^*$, and for endomorphisms $S\otimes I$ and $I\otimes T$ commute ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F4] **Permutation unitaries and sectors.** $U_\pi$ is unitary with $U_\pi(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi^{-1}(n)}$ and $U_\pi U_\sigma=U_{\pi\sigma}$; $U_\pi P_+^{(n)}=P_+^{(n)}U_\pi=P_+^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi P_-^{(n)}=P_-^{(n)}U_\pi=\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)P_-^{(n)}$; the range of $P_+^{(n)}$ is the subspace of vectors fixed by every $U_\pi$, and the range of $P_-^{(n)}$ is the subspace of vectors transforming by $\operatorname{sgn}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F5] **Partial trace.** For endomorphisms $R$ of $V\otimes W$ with $V,W$ finite-dimensional, there is a unique endomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_W R$ of $V$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A)=\operatorname{tr}(R(A\otimes I_W))$ for every $A\in\operatorname{End}(V)$, independent of the orthonormal basis used in its construction; if $R\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}R=1$ then $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=1$ ([[thm-nrqm-composites-finite-partial-trace-and-schmidt]] clauses (a), (b)).

[F6] **Density operators.** A density operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator of trace one ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a), [[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]]).

[F7] **Trace laws.** The trace of an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional space is basis independent, linear, and $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$ ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]], [[prop-trace-is-linear]]); for a trace-class operator $T$ and bounded $S$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(ST)=\operatorname{tr}(TS)$ ([[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F8] **Agreement on dense sets.** Two bounded linear operators from a normed space into a Banach space that agree on a dense subspace are equal ([[thm-extension-of-a-bounded-map-from-a-dense-subspace]]).

[F9] **Unitary conjugation preserves the operator norm.** If $U$ is unitary then $\|UTU^*\|=\|T\|$ ([[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; construct the slot operators by conjugating the first-slot tensor map with a permutation unitary, transport the partial trace through the parenthesisation isometry, and reduce every slot to the first by permutation invariance and cyclicity.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F9].

1.1 [The parenthesisation isometry] For $n=1$, $J_1u=u\otimes1$ is an isometry by [F1], and every tensor in $H\widehat\otimes\mathbb C$ equals $u\otimes1$, so it is surjective. For $n\ge2$, the map $(v_1,\dots,v_n)\mapsto v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$ is multilinear from $H^n$ into $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$, so by [F2] applied to the two parenthesisations of the $n$-fold algebraic tensor product it defines a linear map on the algebraic tensor product, and this linear map preserves inner products on elementary tensors by [F1]: $\langle v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle=\prod_k\langle v_k,w_k\rangle=\langle v_1,w_1\rangle\langle v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n,w_2\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n\rangle$. Since the elementary tensors span a dense subspace and both sides are complete, [F8] and this isometry identity give a linear isometry $J_n$ on the completed tensor powers, and the image is closed and contains all elementary tensors $v_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)$, whose span is dense by [F1]; hence $J_n$ is surjective. This proves (b). [F1, F2, F8, algebra]

1.2 [The first-slot operator] By [F3] the operator $O\otimes I_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}\in\mathcal B(H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)})$ is bounded with $(O\otimes I)(u\otimes w)=Ou\otimes w$. Transporting it through the isometry $J_n$ of clause (b) gives a bounded operator $A_1:=J_n^{-1}(O\otimes I)J_n$ on $H^{\otimes n}$ with $A_1(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=J_n^{-1}(Ov_1\otimes(v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n))=Ov_1\otimes v_2\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$ for all $v_1,\dots,v_n\in H$. [F1, F3, algebra]

1.3 [The zero extension and its symmetry] With $j$ the inclusion of the sector, $\widetilde\rho=j\rho j^*$ restricts to $\rho$ on the sector and vanishes on its orthogonal complement. It is self-adjoint and positive because $\langle\widetilde\rho x,x\rangle=\langle\rho j^*x,j^*x\rangle\ge0$; adjoining an orthonormal basis of the complement to one of the sector gives $\operatorname{tr}\widetilde\rho=\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$, so it is a density operator by [F6]. Since $jj^*=P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi j=\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)j$ by [F4], $\widetilde\rho=P_\sigma^{(n)}\widetilde\rho P_\sigma^{(n)}$ and $U_\pi\widetilde\rho U_\pi^*=\widetilde\rho$ for every $\pi$. A zero sector admits no trace-one endomorphism, so no $\rho$ exists in that case. [F4, F6, F7, algebra]

2.1 [Slot operators and the permutation invariance of their sum] Fix $i$, choose $\pi\in S_n$ with $\pi(1)=i$ and set $O^{(i)}:=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*\in\mathcal B(H^{\otimes n})$; [F9] and step 1.2 give $\|O^{(i)}\|=\|O\otimes I\|\le\|O\|$, and [F3], [F4] give $(O^{(i)})^*=U_\pi J_n^{-1}(O^*\otimes I)J_nU_\pi^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$, so $O=O^*$ gives $O^{(i)}=(O^{(i)})^*$. On elementary tensors, [F4] gives $U_\pi^*(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_{\pi(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes v_{\pi(n)}$; step 1.2 replaces the first factor by $Ov_{\pi(1)}=Ov_i$; and $U_\pi$ then moves that factor to slot $\pi(1)=i$, leaving every other factor in its original slot, so $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_n$. If $\pi'$ is another permutation with $\pi'(1)=i$, then $\tau:=\pi^{-1}\pi'$ fixes $1$ and $U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*$ agrees with $A_1$ on elementary tensors by [F1], [F3], hence equals it by [F8]; thus $U_{\pi'}A_1U_{\pi'}^*=U_\pi U_\tau A_1U_\tau^*U_\pi^*=U_\pi A_1U_\pi^*$ and $O^{(i)}$ is well defined, with the displayed elementary-tensor action. For $\tau\in S_n$ one then has $U_\tau O^{(i)}U_\tau^*=U_{\tau\pi}A_1U_{\tau\pi}^*=O^{(\tau(i))}$, and summing over $i$ with $\tau$ permuting $\{1,\dots,n\}$ gives $U_\tau\Sigma(O)U_\tau^*=\Sigma(O)$ for $\Sigma(O):=\sum_{i=1}^nO^{(i)}$; equivalently $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with every $U_\tau$. Since $P_\sigma^{(n)}=\frac1{n!}\sum_{\pi\in S_n}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)U_\pi$ is a finite linear combination of the $U_\pi$ by [F4], $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(n)}$, so it preserves $\mathfrak H_n^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement and $\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)=P_\sigma^{(n)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(n)}$; this proves (a) and (c). [F1, F3, F4, F8, F9, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 [Reduction to one slot, the trace law and the reduced operator] By steps 1.3 and 2.1 and [F7], for $\pi(1)=i$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho O^{(i)})=\operatorname{tr}(U_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi A_1)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)$. Set $R_n:=J_n\widetilde\rho J_n^{-1}$, an endomorphism of $H\widehat\otimes H^{\otimes(n-1)}$. Its partial trace $\gamma:=\operatorname{Tr}_{H^{\otimes(n-1)}}R_n$ is an endomorphism of $H$ by [F5]. Step 1.2 and [F5], [F7] give $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\Sigma(O))=n\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho A_1)=n\operatorname{tr}(R_n(O\otimes I))=n\operatorname{tr}(\gamma O)$, proving (d). Unitary transport by $J_n$ preserves positivity and trace, so $R_n$ is positive of trace one; [F5] then makes $\gamma$ positive of trace one and hence a density operator on $H$ by [F6]. For the retained slot $i$, use $J_nU_\pi^*$ as the parenthesisation map; its transported state is $J_nU_\pi^*\widetilde\rho U_\pi J_n^{-1}=R_n$ by step 1.3, so its partial trace is the same $\gamma$. More generally the pairing $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma O)=n^{-1}\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\Sigma(O))$ for every $O$ uniquely determines $\gamma$: testing against $O=T_{u,v}$ gives $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma u,v\rangle$ by [[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clause (e), which determines every matrix entry. For $n=1$, $J_1u=u\otimes1$, $P_\sigma^{(1)}=I$ and $\Sigma(O)=O$, so this pairing gives $\gamma=\rho$. This proves (e), including the one-particle boundary. [F4, F5, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Step 1.1 proves (b), step 2.1 proves (a) and (c), and step 3.1 proves (d) and (e); every argument used only the finite-dimensional tensor construction, the permutation sectors, the partial trace and the trace axioms, and no physical object, preparation or measurement entered, which is clause (f). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **Reading of the identities.** The law $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=n\operatorname{tr}(\gamma O)$ says that the mean of the sum of one-body slot operators in the sector preparation is $n$ times the trace pairing of a single one-particle operator with a reduced operator $\gamma$ on the one-particle space. Only the identity is asserted here; its physical reading requires the framework postulates and a declared preparation, and is stated separately.
- **Why the factor $n$ appears.** The sum $\Sigma(O)$ has $n$ slot terms with equal pairings by permutation invariance of the sector state, and $\gamma$ is normalised once, $\operatorname{tr}\gamma=1$; the factor $n$ is the multiplicity of the sum, not a further normalisation.

items.title: Closed formulas for the two-level canonical weights, mean energy, entropy and free energy
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$\varepsilon>0$ and $\beta>0$ be real parameters, let $\mathfrak h$ be a
two-dimensional complex Hilbert space with orthonormal basis
$(u_0,u_1)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]),
and let $H:=T_{u_1,u_1}\varepsilon=\varepsilon\,T_{u_1,u_1}$ be the
self-adjoint operator with eigenvalues $0$ on $\mathbb Cu_0$ and
$\varepsilon$ on $\mathbb Cu_1$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]). Let
$$Z:=\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j},\qquad \rho_\beta:=\frac1Z\sum_{j=0}^{1}e^{-\beta E_j}T_{u_j,u_j},\qquad s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i$$
be the partition sum, canonical operator and entropy of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause
(a), with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $w_i$ the eigenvalues of a density
operator $\rho$ on $\mathfrak h$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). Then:

(a) $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\in(1,2)$, and
$$\rho_\beta=\frac1Z\bigl(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1}\bigr)$$
is a density operator on $\mathfrak h$ that is not the maximally mixed state
$\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$;

(b) the mean energy is the exact identity
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\frac{\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{Z}=\frac{\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1},\qquad 0<\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)<\frac{\varepsilon}{2};$$

(c) the entropy and free energy satisfy
$$s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\frac{\beta\varepsilon}{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}=\log\bigl(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}\bigr)+\frac{\beta\varepsilon\,e^{-\beta\varepsilon}}{1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}},\qquad 0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log 2,$$
and, with $F:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$,
$$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=F ;$$

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are exact algebraic identities for the
declared two-dimensional Hilbert space and the two real parameters
$\varepsilon,\beta>0$; no temperature, thermodynamic, equilibrium or
measurement interpretation is asserted, and the parameter $\beta$ carries no
physical dimension in this lemma.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the real parameters $\varepsilon>0$, $\beta>0$, the two-dimensional complex Hilbert space $\mathfrak h$ with orthonormal basis $(u_0,u_1)$, the operator $H=\varepsilon T_{u_1,u_1}$, and the data $Z$, $\rho_\beta$, $s$ of the statement.

[F1] **Supplied finite Gibbs data.** For the finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H$ with real eigenvalues $E_1,\dots,E_d$ and orthonormal eigenbasis $(v_1,\dots,v_d)$, and $\beta>0$, one has $Z=\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}\in(0,\infty)$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}T_{v_j,v_j}\in\mathcal D$, with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=Z^{-1}\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}E_j$, $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, and for every density operator $\rho$ one has $s(\rho)\le\log d$, with equality if and only if $\rho=d^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

[F2] **Rank-one calculus.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $T_{u,v}^*=T_{v,u}$, $T_{x,x}\ge0$, $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$, and for bounded $B$ one has $BT_{u,v}=T_{Bu,v}$ and $T_{u,v}B=T_{u,B^*v}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a)-(d)); the trace is linear ([[prop-trace-is-linear]]) and $\operatorname{tr}(XY)=\operatorname{tr}(YX)$ ([[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F3] **Real exponential.** $\exp(x)>0$, $\exp(-x)=1/\exp(x)$, and $\exp(x+y)=\exp(x)\exp(y)$ for all real $x,y$ ([[cor-exponential-reciprocal-and-positivity]], [[thm-exponential-addition-formula]]); $\exp$ is strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$ ([[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]). Hence $\exp(0)=\exp(0)^2$ with $\exp(0)>0$, so $\exp(0)=1$, and $\exp(t)>\exp(0)=1$ for every $t>0$.

[F4] **Logarithm.** $\log:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R$ is the inverse function of $\exp$ and satisfies $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$, $\log(1/x)=-\log x$ and $\log 1=0$ ([[def-natural-logarithm]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; instantiate the supplied finite Gibbs formulas at the two eigenvalues $0,\varepsilon$, and control the exponential factor at $\beta\varepsilon>0$ with strict increase, positivity and the reciprocal law.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [Exponential comparison] Since $\beta\varepsilon>0$, strict increase in [F3] gives $\exp(\beta\varepsilon)>\exp(0)=1$, and [F3] gives $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)=1/\exp(\beta\varepsilon)\in(0,1)$; consequently $1<Z=1+\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)<2$. [F3, algebra]

2.1 [The canonical operator] By [F1] with $E_0=0$, $E_1=\varepsilon$ and $(v_1,v_2)=(u_0,u_1)$, $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and $\rho_\beta=Z^{-1}(T_{u_0,u_0}+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}T_{u_1,u_1})\in\mathcal D$, so $\rho_\beta$ is a density operator; its two weights are $Z^{-1}$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}$, which are distinct because $\exp(-\beta\varepsilon)\ne1$ by step 1.1. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Mean energy, entropy and free energy] Using [F2] and $T_{u_0,u_0}T_{u_1,u_1}=\langle u_1,u_0\rangle T_{u_0,u_1}=0$ by orthogonality, and $T_{u_1,u_1}T_{u_1,u_1}=T_{u_1,u_1}$ with $\langle u_1,u_1\rangle=1$, the product $\rho_\beta H$ equals $\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}Z^{-1}T_{u_1,u_1}$, so [F2] gives $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/Z$; by step 1.1, $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/Z=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$ lies in $(0,\varepsilon/2)$. By [F1], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z$, so $s(\rho_\beta)=\log Z+\beta\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)=\log(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})+\beta\varepsilon e^{-\beta\varepsilon}/(1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon})$; by [F1] and [F2], $0\le s(\rho_\beta)<\log2$ because $\rho_\beta\ne\tfrac12\mathrm{id}$ by step 2.1. Finally $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho_\beta)=-\beta^{-1}\log Z=F$ with $F$ as defined. This proves (b) and (c), and step 2.1 proved (a). [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a), step 3.1 proves (b) and (c), and every identity is an algebraic consequence of the supplied finite-dimensional formulas and the real exponential and logarithm laws, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **High- and low-temperature expectations.** By [F3], $0<e^{-\beta\varepsilon}<1$ and $e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ decreases strictly as the product $\beta\varepsilon$ grows, so the upper level is suppressed in the regime of large $\beta\varepsilon$, while the bound $s<\log2$ of clause (c) shows that the entropy stays below the maximal mixed-state value for every finite $\beta>0$. The lemma asserts only these algebraic facts about the weights; it identifies no physical temperature with $\beta$.
- **Use.** The formulas are the exact two-level data used by the examples and the thought experiment of the companion page; the physical reading of $\beta$ as an inverse temperature, and of $\rho_\beta$ as a thermal preparation, is supplied separately by the framework's equilibrium postulate.

items.title: CC realization of the bounded spatial operator on a finite-component H² domain
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers $N,M\ge1$, $a>0$, and a real measurable function $V:\mathbb R^{3N}\to\mathbb R$ with $v=\operatorname{ess\,sup}|V|<\infty$. Put
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad Y=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
where the vector space, pairing and Sobolev norm are the finite component sums of the scalar conventions of [[def-hilbert-space]], [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Use the componentwise Plancherel unitary of [[thm-plancherel]], with the negative-sign $2\pi$ convention of [[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]]. Define
$$w(\xi)=4\pi^2a|\xi|^2,\qquad K=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_w\mathcal F_2,\qquad D(K)=\{u:w\mathcal F_2u\in\mathcal H\}.$$
Then $D(K)=Y$, and $Ku=-a\Delta u$ for every $u\in Y$, with the distributional Laplacian acting componentwise. The operator
$$H=K+M_V=-a\Delta+V,\qquad D(H)=Y,$$
is densely defined and self-adjoint on exactly $Y$, and $H\ge-v$. Both $K$ and $H$ have graph norms equivalent to the stated Sobolev norm, and $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is a core for both. For $z=\pm i\mu$ with $\mu>v$, there is the concrete two-sided inverse
$$R_H(z)=(H-z)^{-1}=R_0(z)\sum_{k\ge0}(-M_VR_0(z))^k,\qquad R_0(z)=\mathcal F_2^{-1}M_{(w-z)^{-1}}\mathcal F_2,$$
with range exactly $Y$ and $\|R_H(z)\|\le(\mu-v)^{-1}$.

This realizes the equal-mass bounded spatial operator used at fixed $N$ by setting $a=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and any finite spin multiplicity $M$; for an $N$-fold spin-$s$ tensor the full multiplicity is $M=(2s+1)^N$. The lemma makes no statement about Coulomb potentials, unequal-mass operators, thermodynamic limits, or physical assignments. It uses no Axiom of Choice or Kato–Rellich theorem.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** CC; $N,M,a,V,v,\mathcal H,Y,w$ as above. Pairings are linear in the first argument.

[F1] Under CC, the scalar Plancherel transform is a surjective complex-linear isometry preserving the pairing ([[thm-plancherel]], Statement). Under CC, $W^{2,2}$ equals the weighted Fourier space, with its Sobolev norm equivalent to $\|(1+|\xi|^2)\mathcal F_2u\|_2$, and the $2\pi$ derivative multiplier is $\mathcal F_2(D^\alpha u)=(2\pi i\xi)^\alpha\mathcal F_2u$ when the weak derivative is in $L^2$ ([[thm-fourier-characterisation-of-integer-order-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]], Statement (1),(2), [[lem-weak-derivatives-are-polynomial-fourier-multipliers]], Statement). Finite component sums preserve these identities and norm equivalences.

[F2] For a densely defined operator, the adjoint domain consists of vectors admitting a representing vector in its pairing identity; a symmetric operator is self-adjoint exactly when its adjoint has the same domain and action ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]). A self-adjoint operator is closed.

[F3] Under CC, $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$ is dense in $W^{2,2}$ and in $L^2$ ([[cor-compactly-supported-smooth-functions-are-dense-in-wkp-of-rn]], Statement with $(k,p)=(2,2)$ and $(0,2)$). The same holds for finitely many components. Dominated convergence holds for the squared cutoff tails ([[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

## Proof

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]–[F3].

1.1 [Concrete multiplier, including the adjoint domain] For any real finite-valued measurable function $b$ on $\mathbb R^{3N}$, multiplication on $D(M_b)=\{f:bf\in\mathcal H\}$ is densely defined: $f_L=\mathbf1_{|b|\le L}f$ belongs to this domain and tends to $f$ by dominated convergence. It is symmetric because $b$ is real and the pairings are integrable by Cauchy–Schwarz. If $g\in D(M_b^*)$ with representing vector $h$, every $f\in\mathcal H$ supported on $E_L=\{|b|\le L\}$ belongs to the multiplier domain and satisfies $\langle f,bg-h\rangle=0$ on that set. The vector $\mathbf1_{E_L}(bg-h)$ lies in $\mathcal H$, so testing with that vector proves $h=bg$ a.e. on $E_L$. Increasing the integer $L$ covers the space up to null sets, proving $bg=h\in\mathcal H$ and $g\in D(M_b)$. Conversely the symmetry identity gives every vector of $D(M_b)$ in the adjoint domain with adjoint value $bg$. Thus $M_b$ is self-adjoint on the exact maximal domain, including for the weight $w$. This proof is valid for the finite vector-valued space by its component-sum pairing; it makes no arbitrary family of choices. [given, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Fourier transfer, exact H² and normalization] Apply the componentwise unitary $\mathcal F_2$ from [F1] to step 1.1 with $b=w$. For a vector $y$ in the adjoint domain of $K$, changing variables $f=\mathcal F_2u$ in its representing functional gives $\mathcal F_2y\in D(M_w^*)=D(M_w)$ with the corresponding adjoint value; the converse follows from symmetry. Hence $K$ is self-adjoint on $\mathcal F_2^{-1}D(M_w)$. Since $w=4\pi^2a|\xi|^2$ with $a>0$, $1+w$ is bounded above and below by positive multiples of $1+|\xi|^2$. For $u\in L^2$, $w\mathcal F_2u\in L^2$ therefore holds exactly when $(1+|\xi|^2)\mathcal F_2u\in L^2$, which is $u\in Y$ by [F1]. Moreover $\|\mathcal F_2u\|_2+\|w\mathcal F_2u\|_2$ is equivalent to $\|(1+w)\mathcal F_2u\|_2$ by the triangle inequality and nonnegativity of $w$, and hence to $\|u\|_Y$. This proves graph-norm equivalence. The weak-derivative multiplier in [F1] gives $\mathcal F_2(-a\Delta u)=4\pi^2a|\xi|^2\mathcal F_2u$, proving the exact differential action for all $u\in Y$. Finally $\langle Ku,u\rangle=\int w\|\mathcal F_2u\|^2\ge0$, with integrability by Cauchy–Schwarz. [step 1.1, F1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Explicit perturbed inverses on the fixed domain] Multiplication by $V$ is bounded and self-adjoint on $\mathcal H$, with norm at most $v$, since $V$ is real and essentially bounded. Thus $H=K+M_V$ is symmetric on the dense $Y$ and is closed there: if $u_l\to u$ and $Hu_l\to h$, boundedness gives $Ku_l\to h-M_Vu$, and closedness of $K$ gives $u\in Y$ with $Hu=h$. For $z=\pm i\mu$, the concrete multiplier $(w-z)^{-1}$ is bounded by $\mu^{-1}$ and $|w/(w-z)|\le1$. Therefore $R_0(z)$ maps $\mathcal H$ into $Y$ and satisfies both inverse equations of $K-z$, with range exactly $Y$. On $Y$ the correctly ordered factorization is $H-z=(I+M_VR_0(z))(K-z)$. Since $\|M_VR_0(z)\|\le v/\mu<1$, the geometric series in the statement is the inverse of the first factor: finite-sum multiplication leaves a remainder tending to zero in norm. The bounded operator space is complete, because an operator-norm Cauchy sequence has a bounded pointwise limit on the complete target and the same uniform Cauchy estimate gives operator-norm convergence. Thus $R_H(z)$ exists, maps into $Y$, and its two ordered inverse equations follow from the factorization. Surjectivity of this range onto $Y$ follows from the second inverse equation. Its norm is at most $\mu^{-1}/(1-v/\mu)=(\mu-v)^{-1}$. [step 2.1, F1, F2, construct, algebra]

4.1 [Self-adjointness without an AC perturbation theorem] Let $y\in D(H^*)$. By step 3.1, $H-i\mu:Y\to\mathcal H$ is onto; solve $(H-i\mu)x=(H^*-i\mu)y$ with its explicit inverse, so $x\in Y$. Symmetry implies $H^*x=Hx$, whence $y-x\in\ker(H^*-i\mu)$. For a densely defined operator with first-linear pairing, this kernel is $\operatorname{ran}(H+i\mu)^\perp$, directly from the adjoint identity. The other inverse from step 3.1 makes that range all of $\mathcal H$, so $y=x\in Y$. Since $H\subseteq H^*$ by symmetry, the adjoint domains and actions are equal, proving self-adjointness on exactly $Y$. Also $\langle Hu,u\rangle=\langle Ku,u\rangle+\int V\|u\|^2\ge-v\|u\|^2$ for every $u\in Y$, proving the claimed lower bound. Only the two explicit imaginary resolvents were used. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F2, algebra]

5.1 [Graph norms, cores and scope] For $u\in Y$, boundedness of $V$ gives $\|Hu\|\le\|Ku\|+v\|u\|$ and $\|Ku\|\le\|Hu\|+v\|u\|$. Thus the graph norms of $H$ and $K$ are equivalent, and step 2.1 identifies both with the Sobolev norm. The finite-component smooth density from [F3] therefore makes $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ graph dense in the exact domain of each operator, which is precisely the core claim. Steps 1.1–4.1 supply the self-adjointness, exact differential action, lower bound and explicit inverses. All primitive suppliers used here assume CC; neither an AC multiplier theorem nor Kato–Rellich nor any assertion concerning a singular potential or an arbitrary spin basis was invoked. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra] ∎

items.title: Finite spin components of an N-fold spatial tensor product
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $N,r\ge1$ be integers, $H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r)$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$, and $M=r^N$. In the product basis $e_a=e_{a_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_N}$ indexed by $a\in\{1,\dots,r\}^N$, identify $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$ and write $\mathcal L_N=L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$. Then:

(a) There is a unique unitary $\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\to\mathcal L_N$ such that
$$[\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(x_1,\dots,x_N)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j}.$$

(b) For $\pi\in S_N$, let $U_\pi$ be the permutation of the complete one-particle factors and $R_\pi e_a=e_{a_{\pi^{-1}(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{a_{\pi^{-1}(N)}}$ the permutation of spin factors. With $X^\pi=(x_{\pi(1)},\dots,x_{\pi(N)})$, the conjugate permutation is
$$\mathcal U_\pi:=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1},\qquad (\mathcal U_\pi\Psi)(X)=R_\pi\Psi(X^\pi).$$
In particular $[\mathcal U_\pi\Psi]_a(X)=\Psi_{(a_{\pi(1)},\dots,a_{\pi(N)})}(X^\pi)$; averaging this combined action gives $\mathcal P_\pm=\Theta_NP_\pm^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$.

(c) The component domain $\mathcal D_N=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ is the set of tuples with every scalar component in $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)$. If a scalar self-adjoint $T$ has this scalar domain and its domain is preserved by every spatial block permutation, commuting with that permutation on the domain, its finite direct sum $T_M\Psi=(T\Psi_a)_a$ on $\mathcal D_N$ is self-adjoint, retains every scalar lower bound $T\ge cI$, and commutes with the combined permutations on that domain. The restrictions of $T_M$ to $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, with domain $\mathcal D_N\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$, are self-adjoint when the sector is nonzero; on the zero sector the unique zero operator has domain $\{0\}$.

(d) For matrices $A_j\in\mathcal B(\mathbb C^r)$, the constant spin action $A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N$ preserves $\mathcal D_N$ and commutes with $T_M$. Its permutation covariance is
$$R_\pi(A_1\otimes\cdots\otimes A_N)R_\pi^{-1}=A_{\pi^{-1}(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes A_{\pi^{-1}(N)}.$$
Thus a common internal unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ commutes with $\mathcal U_\pi$, preserves both sectors and commutes with their restricted operators. This is a tensor identity and asserts no physical spin-statistics assignment. For $r=1$ all spin actions are scalar and $\Theta_N$ is the iterated scalar product unitary; for $N=1$ it is the identity component identification.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $N,r,H,\mathcal S_N,M,\mathcal L_N$, the product spin basis, and in (c) the scalar self-adjoint $T$ with domain $W^{2,2}$ and spatial permutation invariance.

[F1] The scalar Euclidean product map is unitary and permits finite component sums ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]] Statement); iterating it gives the scalar N-factor product map. The component identification is unitary for every Euclidean dimension and finite component count ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] (a), (b)).

[F2] Tensor pairings multiply, elementary tensors span densely, and spin product bases are orthonormal; bounded factor maps extend with their tensor action and adjoints ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]]). Factor permutations and their symmetric/sign averages are unitary and orthogonal projections respectively ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] (a)-(c)).

[F3] A self-adjoint operator invariant on its domain under a unitary finite-group permutation representation restricts self-adjointly to each nonzero symmetric/sign sector ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] (a)-(d)); the scalar-only application (e) is not needed for a spin sector.

## Proof

**Given:** The data of the Statement and [F1]-[F3].

1.1 [Finite component product unitary] Resolve each one-particle vector into its $r$ components by [F1]. On the dense span of vectors $(g_1e_{a_1})\otimes\cdots\otimes(g_Ne_{a_N})$, send this vector to the function $(\prod_jg_j(x_j))e_a$. Inner products of such vectors are the product of the scalar pairings times $\prod_j\delta_{a_jb_j}$ by [F2]; their image pairings have exactly the same value by the iterated scalar unitary [F1]. Linearity therefore gives a well-defined isometry on this dense span. Its image is dense: in each of the finitely many components the scalar products span densely by [F1]. The isometry extends to the completion; its range is closed by completeness and dense, hence all of $\mathcal L_N$. Expansion of the finite components gives the formula in (a), and equality on a dense span gives uniqueness. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 [Combined permutation] On the component product vectors of step 1.1, applying $U_\pi$ replaces the factor in slot $j$ by the former factor in slot $\pi^{-1}(j)$. Evaluating the product formula gives $(\mathcal U_\pi\Psi)(X)=R_\pi\Psi(X^\pi)$, including the displayed component-index formula. Both operators are bounded unitaries, so the equality extends by density. Conjugating the finite averages of [F2] gives $\mathcal P_\pm$; this simultaneously permutes spatial blocks and spin slots. [step 1.1, F2, algebra]

3.1 [Finite component domain and self-adjointness] Since there are finitely many components, the definition of weak derivatives shows $\mathcal D_N=(W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C))^{\oplus M}$: derivative testing and integrability hold componentwise in both directions, and all norms are finite sums. The direct sum $T_M$ is dense and symmetric. A vector $\eta$ lies in $D(T_M^*)$ precisely when testing separately in each component puts $\eta_a\in D(T^*)=D(T)$ for every $a$; conversely these finitely many adjoint values give a vector in $\mathcal L_N$. Thus $D(T_M^*)=\mathcal D_N$ and $T_M^*=T_M$. If $T\ge cI$, summing the scalar quadratic inequalities gives $T_M\ge cI$. The hypothesis on scalar spatial permutations gives domain preservation and commutation for their componentwise action; $R_\pi$ is a constant permutation of finitely many components, so it preserves the domain and commutes with $T_M$ too. Their combined action in step 2.1 has both properties. [given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Sector restrictions] Apply [F3] to the self-adjoint $T_M$ of step 3.1 and the combined representation from step 2.1. It gives reduction and self-adjointness on every nonzero $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\pm$ with exactly the stated intersection domain. If a sector is zero, its Hilbert space and dense operator domain are both $\{0\}$, so its unique operator is its own adjoint. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 [Spin covariance and edge cases] A constant spin matrix makes finite linear combinations of the scalar components, so it preserves $\mathcal D_N$ and commutes with the componentwise scalar $T_M$. On elementary spin tensors the conjugation by $R_\pi$ reorders the matrices to $A_{\pi^{-1}(j)}$ in slot $j$; by linearity this is the displayed covariance on all of $\mathcal S_N$. For a common $A$, the reordering leaves $A^{\otimes N}$ unchanged, so it commutes with each combined permutation and its averages; if $A$ is unitary the inverse has the same properties, proving onto preservation of both sectors and their domains. At $r=1$ the sole component is scalar, and at $N=1$ the product formula is the original vector-valued function. These establish (d) and all stated branches. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, F2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Fixed-particle-number occupation bases and the countable-mode partition criterion
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space with a supplied countably infinite orthonormal basis $(e_j)_{j\ge1}$, let $N\ge1$ be an integer, and let $\varepsilon_j\in\mathbb R$ with $\varepsilon_j\ge b$ for a fixed $b\in\mathbb R$. Use the completed tensor power and permutation-sector projections of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] and [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], and write $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma:=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ for $\sigma\in\{+,-\}$. Then:

(a) For every finitely supported sequence $n=(n_j)_{j\ge1}$ of nonnegative integers with $\sum_jn_j=N$, put $\operatorname{orb}(n):=\{(i_1,\ldots,i_N):\#\{k:i_k=j\}=n_j\text{ for every }j\}$ and
$$b_n^+:=|\operatorname{orb}(n)|^{-1/2}\sum_{i\in\operatorname{orb}(n)}e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}.$$
For every $N$-element subset $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ of the positive integers, put
$$b_J^-:=\frac1{\sqrt{N!}}\sum_{\pi\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\pi)e_{j_{\pi(1)}}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_{\pi(N)}}.$$
These are orthonormal bases of the symmetric and antisymmetric sectors respectively. Denote their countable index sets by $\mathcal C_N^+$ and $\mathcal C_N^-$, and write $b_c^\sigma$ for the corresponding vector. Define $E_n:=\sum_jn_j\varepsilon_j$ and $E_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$.

(b) The fixed-$N$ free energy operator is the self-adjoint diagonal operator
$$D(H_N^\sigma):=\left\{\psi=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}a_cb_c^\sigma:\sum_c|E_c|^2|a_c|^2<\infty\right\},\qquad H_N^\sigma\psi:=\sum_cE_ca_cb_c^\sigma.$$
It is bounded below by $Nb$, and is the closure of its action on finite occupation sums. On elementary tensors of modes it agrees with the restriction of the labelled energy sum $\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}$, with the same diagonal-domain closure. Its spectral PVM is
$$E_N^\sigma(B)\psi=\sum_c\mathbf1_B(E_c)a_cb_c^\sigma.$$

(c) For $\beta>0$, let $q_j:=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}>0$, so $q_j\le e^{-\beta b}$. Define the extended positive trace of a bounded positive operator as its nonnegative diagonal sum in the supplied occupation basis; its independence of any other supplied orthonormal basis is proved below. With this trace (allowed to be $+\infty$),
$$Z_N^+(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^+}=h_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1\le\cdots\le i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N},$$
$$Z_N^-(\beta):=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H_N^-}=e_N(q):=\sum_{1\le i_1<\cdots<i_N}q_{i_1}\cdots q_{i_N}.$$
All sums are nonnegative-series sums. For either sign,
$$\left(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k\right)\sum_{j=N}^\infty q_j\le Z_N^\sigma(\beta)\le\left(\sum_{j=1}^\infty q_j\right)^N.$$
For $N=1$ the product is $1$, the tail starts at $1$, and both partition sums equal $\sum_jq_j$. Consequently, for every fixed $N\ge1$ and either statistics,
$$0<Z_N^\sigma(\beta)<\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_j e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}<\infty.$$
The bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$ is trace class exactly in this case, and its ordinary trace then equals the displayed occupation sum. This is a fixed-$N$ criterion, not a trace over all particle numbers.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the supplied basis, $N\ge1$, the lower bound $b$, real energies $\varepsilon_j\ge b$, and $\beta>0$ in clause (c).

[F1] Completed tensor products have dense algebraic tensor products and the elementary-tensor inner-product formula; the permutation projections are bounded orthogonal projections acting by finite permutation sums ([[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]]).

[F2] In each finite prefix $H_m:=\operatorname{span}\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}$ the Slater vectors indexed by $N$-element subsets form an orthonormal antisymmetric basis, and the orbit sums are a nonzero orthogonal symmetric basis ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] (a)-(c)).

[F3] Cauchy-Schwarz controls square-summable coefficient pairings ([[thm-cauchy-schwarz-in-an-inner-product-space]]). A complete orthonormal family gives Parseval and norm-convergent coordinate expansion ([[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]). The adjoint of a densely defined operator is characterized by $\langle Tx,y\rangle=\langle x,T^*y\rangle$, and equality with the adjoint means self-adjointness ([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).

[F4] A PVM is strongly countably additive; integration of bounded Borel functions gives the corresponding bounded operator and its scalar spectral integrals ([[def-projection-valued-measure]], [[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). The unbounded identity integral has the scalar squared-moment domain and is obtained by bounded coordinate truncations ([[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]], [[lem-unbounded-pvm-integral-is-well-defined-and-closed]]).

[F5] Finite-rank operators are compact and their operator-norm limits are compact ([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]). An absolutely summable nuclear series defines a trace-class operator, with trace equal to the sum of its rank-one traces; a trace-class operator has an absolutely summable diagonal in every supplied orthonormal basis ([[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]], [[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; exhaust the supplied basis by finite prefixes, compute the unbounded diagonal adjoint on coordinates, and compare nonnegative fixed-N occupation sums.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [Product basis and finite-prefix exhaustion] The tensors $e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ are orthonormal by [F1]. Their span is dense: approximate each factor of an elementary tensor by its finite basis truncation using [F3]; the tensor norm formula and the telescoping difference of two products show convergence of these approximations, and finite sums of elementary tensors are dense by [F1]. Every finite collection of words is contained in some $H_m^{\otimes N}$. Since each $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is bounded, its images of this dense word span are dense in its range. In the finite prefix, these images span precisely the finite Slater or orbit-sum basis of [F2]. A word in $\operatorname{orb}(n)$ uses only finitely many modes, and the orbit consists of distinct orthonormal product vectors, so its sum has norm squared $|\operatorname{orb}(n)|>0$. Thus its displayed normalization agrees in every larger prefix. The finite-prefix Slater vectors likewise agree in every larger prefix. Any pair of proposed occupation vectors lies in a common prefix, where [F2] gives orthogonality; the normalized vectors have norm one. Their span is dense in the sector by the projection argument, proving (a). The index sets are countable because they are countable unions of finite prefix index sets. [F1, F2, F3, algebra, construct]

2.1 [Diagonal domain and self-adjointness] Write either sector in the orthonormal coordinates of step 1.1. The specified domain contains every finite coordinate vector, hence is dense. For a vector in that domain, Parseval makes the defining energy series converge. If $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain, with adjoint value $z$, testing against each $b_c^\sigma$ gives $z_c=E_cy_c$ because $E_c$ is real. Since $z$ is square summable, $\sum_c|E_cy_c|^2<\infty$, so $y$ belongs to the specified domain. Conversely, if that sum is finite, Cauchy-Schwarz applied to the square-summable coefficient families gives $\langle H_N^\sigma x,y\rangle=\langle x,H_N^\sigma y\rangle$ for every domain vector $x$, so $y$ belongs to the adjoint domain with the stated value. The domains and values agree, proving self-adjointness by [F3]. Since every $E_c\ge Nb$, the absolutely convergent energy quadratic sum is at least $Nb\|x\|^2$. Finite coordinate truncations converge in both norm and graph norm since both square-sum tails vanish, so finite occupation sums are a core and the operator is their diagonal closure. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Labelled energy and spectral measure] The same coordinate-domain construction on the product-word basis defines a self-adjoint labelled operator with energies $\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k}$, agreeing with the free slot-energy sum on finite mode words. Every permutation of a word has the same energy, so its domain and action commute with each permutation unitary and the projections [F1]. Their sector restrictions have exactly the occupation energies and domain of step 2.1. For the displayed $E_N^\sigma(B)$, the projection and intersection identities follow coordinatewise; for disjoint $B_l$, the tails of the square-summable coordinates give strong countable additivity and total mass $I$, so it is a PVM. The scalar measure of a vector $\psi=\sum_ca_cb_c^\sigma$ is $\sum_c|a_c|^2\delta_{E_c}$, so [F4] gives the identity-integral domain exactly $\sum_cE_c^2|a_c|^2<\infty$; bounded spectral truncations converge to the displayed coordinate action there. This PVM is also uniquely determined by that operator: if another PVM represents it, the zero norm of $(H_N^\sigma-E_c)b_c^\sigma$ forces its scalar measure at $b_c^\sigma$ to be supported at $E_c$. Its projections therefore act as $\mathbf1_B(E_c)$ on every $b_c^\sigma$, and density gives equality on the whole sector. For the exponential, use the bounded Borel function $g(a)=e^{-\beta\max\{a,Nb\}}$ on $\mathbb R$; it agrees with $e^{-\beta a}$ on the support of this PVM. [F4] therefore gives the bounded positive operator with eigenvalues $e^{-\beta E_c}\le e^{-\beta Nb}$, namely $e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}$. This proves (b) and identifies the exponential used in (c). [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Extended trace and occupation sums] Put $r_c:=e^{-\beta E_c}$, a bounded positive family. In the supplied occupation basis the extended positive trace is $\sum_cr_c$. This value is basis independent even when infinite: if $(v_l)$ is any other orthonormal basis, then $\sum_l\langle e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}v_l,v_l\rangle=\sum_l\sum_cr_c|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=\sum_cr_c$, since nonnegative-series sums can be interchanged as suprema over finite subsums, and Parseval gives $\sum_l|\langle v_l,b_c^\sigma\rangle|^2=1$. A Bose occupation sequence has a unique sorted word $i_1\le\cdots\le i_N$, and a Fermi subset has a unique increasing word; $e^{-\beta E_c}$ is the product of the corresponding $q_j$. Thus the trace equals $h_N(q)$ or $e_N(q)$ as stated. If the sum is finite, the series of rank-one operators $\sum_cr_c\langle\cdot,b_c^\sigma\rangle b_c^\sigma$ is nuclear and converges in operator norm to the exponential: its norm tail is at most the summable scalar tail. Its finite-rank partial sums and [F5] first give compactness, and the nuclear criterion then gives trace class and the ordinary trace formula. Conversely trace class forces the diagonal sum to be finite by [F5]. [F3, F5, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Upper and lower bounds and finiteness] Let $Q:=\sum_jq_j\in(0,\infty]$. The sum over all ordered words of length $N$ is $Q^N$: on the first $m$ modes it is $(\sum_{j\le m}q_j)^N$, and every finite collection of words is contained in one such prefix. The nondecreasing and strictly increasing index sets are subsets of the ordered-word set, giving $Z_N^\sigma\le Q^N$. For $N\ge2$, configurations selecting modes $1,\ldots,N-1$ once each and one additional mode $j\ge N$ are valid for both statistics, distinct as $j$ varies, and have weight $(\prod_{k=1}^{N-1}q_k)q_j$. Their sum gives the lower bound. For $N=1$, every configuration is the single mode $j$, so both traces equal $Q$; the empty product is $1$ and the tail starts at $1$. For any $N$, the lower-bound coefficient is strictly positive and finite, and the omitted initial segment of $Q$ is finite. Hence $Q=\infty$ forces $Z_N^\sigma=\infty$, whereas $Q<\infty$ gives $Z_N^\sigma<\infty$ by the upper bound. The single configuration $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ has positive weight for either sign, so both traces are strictly positive. This proves all of (c). No sum over particle numbers or full-Fock product formula is used. [step 4.1, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Spectral first moments and trace products with a density operator
items.statement:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator on a nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $E_A$ be its spectral PVM, let $\rho$ be a density operator, and set $\mu_\rho^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$. Then:

(a) The finite first mean is defined exactly under the absolute-first-moment condition
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)<\infty,$$
and its value is $m:=\int a\,d\mu_\rho^A(a)$. For every positive-eigenvalue expansion $\rho=\sum_kw_kT_{u_k,u_k}$ of [[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a), with $w_k>0$ and $\sum_kw_k=1$, one has
$$\int|a|\,d\mu_\rho^A=\sum_kw_k\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k},\qquad m=\sum_kw_k\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}.$$
The first identity allows infinity; the second is asserted under the stated integrability condition and converges absolutely. This condition does not require $u_k\in D(A)$.

(b) If $A$ is bounded, the condition in (a) holds automatically and
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A).$$

(c) Suppose the condition in (a) holds and the **literal product** $A\rho$ is defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class; thus $\rho(H)\subset D(A)$ and $T:=A\rho\in\mathcal S_1(H)$. Then
$$m=\operatorname{tr}(T).$$
Moreover the densely defined product $\rho A$ has bounded closure $T^*$, that closure is trace class, and $\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho A})=m$. This is a conditional trace identity for defined trace-class products. The existence of the mean alone does not assert any of these unbounded-operator product hypotheses.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The choice hypotheses, $A,E_A,\rho,\mu_\rho^A$, and in (c) the explicitly stated literal-product assumptions.

[F1] The density eigenexpansion has positive weights and orthonormal vectors, converges in trace norm, and gives $\mu_\rho^A(B)=\sum_kw_kE_{A,u_k}(B)$. For $u\in D(A)$, $\int a\,dE_{A,u}=\langle Au,u\rangle$; absolute first integrability alone is equivalent to $u\in D(|A|^{1/2})$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] (a)-(c)).

[F2] Nonnegative monotone limits commute with integrals, and integrable domination permits limits of signed integrals ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]], [[thm-dominated-convergence]]).

[F3] Bounded Borel spectral integrals agree with their scalar spectral integrals ([[thm-bounded-borel-pvm-integral]]). Bounded multiplication of a density eigenexpansion gives $\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$ and bounded cyclicity gives $\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-nuclear-bounded-cyclicity]]).

[F4] A trace-class operator has its trace as an absolutely convergent diagonal in a supplied Hilbert basis; it also has a nuclear representation whose rank-one traces sum to its trace ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]], [[lem-nuclear-series-characterizes-trace-norm]]). Under AC, a chain of orthonormal families containing a given family has its orthonormal union as an upper bound, so [[thm-zorn]] provides a maximal extension. Its orthogonal complement is zero by maximality, hence it is complete by [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]]. Coordinate expansion is [[thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion]]. Finite-rank maps and their operator-norm limits are compact ([[lem-finite-rank-operators-are-compact]], [[thm-norm-limit-of-compact-operators-is-compact]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; integrate the density eigenexpansion and compare it with correctly defined trace products.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]-[F4].

1.1 [First-moment expansion] By [F1] the outcome measure is the countable weighted sum of the scalar measures. This gives $\int g\,d\mu_\rho^A=\sum_kw_k\int g\,dE_{A,u_k}$ first for nonnegative simple functions by the measure identity and finite linearity, and then for all nonnegative measurable $g$ by increasing simple approximation and [F2]; the nonnegative sums interchange as increasing finite subsums. Taking $g=|a|$ gives the first identity in (a), including infinity. When it is finite, both positive and negative parts are integrable, so subtracting their two finite sums gives $m=\sum_kw_k\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}$ with $\sum_kw_k|\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}|\le\sum_kw_k\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k}<\infty$. For each positive $w_k$, only absolute first integrability is forced; [F1] identifies its form domain, without requiring the operator-square moment. This proves (a). [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [Bounded observable] If $A$ is bounded, every $u_k$ is in $D(A)$, and Cauchy-Schwarz for the scalar probability measure gives $\int|a|\,dE_{A,u_k}\le(\int a^2\,dE_{A,u_k})^{1/2}=\|Au_k\|\le\|A\|$ by [F1] ([[cor-cauchy-schwarz-inequality-for-l-two]]). Step 1.1 therefore bounds the first absolute moment by $\|A\|$. Each $u_k$ is in $D(A)$ and [F1] gives $\int a\,dE_{A,u_k}=\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$. Thus step 1.1 and the bounded trace formula [F3] give $m=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$. This proves (b). [F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 [Literal trace-class left product] Under (c), $\rho u_k=w_ku_k\in D(A)$ and $w_k>0$, so each $u_k\in D(A)$ and $Tu_k=w_kAu_k$. Complete the orthonormal eigenfamily by an orthonormal basis of its perpendicular subspace using the already assumed AC. The density eigenexpansion shows $\rho=0$ on that perpendicular subspace, so $T=0$ there. The trace diagonal formula [F4] therefore gives $\operatorname{tr}(T)=\sum_k\langle Tu_k,u_k\rangle=\sum_kw_k\langle Au_k,u_k\rangle$. Step 1.1 and [F1] identify this absolutely convergent scalar sum with $m$. This proof uses the literal-product hypothesis to obtain $u_k\in D(A)$; it does not infer that hypothesis from first-moment existence. [F1, F4, step 1.1, choose, algebra]

3.1 [Closure of the right product] For $x\in D(A)$ and arbitrary $y$, self-adjointness of $A$ and $\rho$ gives $\langle\rho Ax,y\rangle=\langle Ax,\rho y\rangle=\langle x,A\rho y\rangle=\langle x,Ty\rangle=\langle T^*x,y\rangle$, so $\rho A$ agrees with the bounded $T^*$ on the dense domain $D(A)$. Its graph closure is all of the graph of $T^*$: approximate any $x$ by $x_l\in D(A)$ and use boundedness of $T^*$, while its closed graph contains every graph limit from that restriction. A nuclear representation $T=\sum_jT_{v_j,z_j}$ gives $T^*=\sum_jT_{z_j,v_j}$ with the same summable nuclear norms; the operator-norm convergence of these finite-rank partial sums first gives compactness, and then the nuclear criterion gives trace class and [F4] gives $\operatorname{tr}(T^*)=\overline{\operatorname{tr}(T)}=m$, since the spectral integral $m$ is real. This proves (c), without invoking cyclicity for unbounded multipliers. [F4, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: The declared fixed-N many-body model: species sector, one-particle data, interaction and the sector energy observable
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings, units and choice hypotheses.** Adopt the state and
composition postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the
observable and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4), the non-relativistic kinematics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]] (P5)
and the identical-particle and spin postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] (P6), in the state
reading of [[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]], the observable
reading of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
evolution reading of [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] and
the sector vocabulary of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]].
Let a **declared species sector** with one-particle space $H$, mass $m>0$
(kg), spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and statistics choice
$\sigma\in\{+,-\}$ be given as in that definition, in the massive spin-$s$
one-particle reading of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]; fix an integer
$N\ge1$ and let $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq
H^{\otimes N}$ be the declared $N$-particle sector. All quantities below are
read in the SI conventions and units of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] (energies in joules). Assume the
Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]); the Axiom of Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) is assumed only in the Coulomb realization of
clause (d)(ii), where it is the choice hypothesis of the cited self-adjointness
theorem.

**(b) Declared one-particle data.** The model declares a one-particle
**energy operator** in one of the two following realizations.

(i) *Spatial realization.* The one-particle space is
$H=L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and, with $\hbar>0$ the reduced Planck
constant, the model declares a **kinetic operator** $K_1:=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta$
on $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$ and a real, measurable, bounded
**external potential** $V_{\mathrm{ext}}:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ of essential
supremum $\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty<\infty$; the declared one-particle
operator is $h:=K_1+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(Q)$, self-adjoint by [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]] with $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and $a_1=\hbar^2/(2m)$, with domain
$W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^{2s+1})$. A more singular declared
$V_{\mathrm{ext}}$, such as $-g/|x|$, is used only through a separate
self-adjointness statement, which the model must supply before the operator is
read as an observable.

(ii) *Finite-mode realization.* A finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space
$K$ of dimension $d\ge1$ with a declared orthonormal basis
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$ ([[def-hilbert-space]]) is declared together with a
self-adjoint **one-particle operator** $h\in\mathcal B(K)$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]).
Here the one-particle space of the species is $K$, and the assignment of the
modes $f_j$ to a laboratory mode family is a tested identification under the
preparation and apparatus postulate P7, not part of the definition.

**(c) Declared interaction.** The model declares a **pair interaction** in the
matching realization.

(i) *Bounded interaction.* In the spatial realization let
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$ be real, measurable, bounded with
$W(-z)=W(z)$ for almost every $z$ and $\|W\|_\infty<\infty$. In the
finite-mode realization let $W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ be
self-adjoint with $U_{(12)}WU_{(12)}=W$, where $U_{(12)}$ is the exchange
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (a)
in the tensor square $\widehat{K\otimes K}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]. The interaction strength
constants entering $W$ are empirical model parameters with their uncertainties
in the sense of P6 clause (iii).

(ii) *Coulomb interaction.* In the spatial realization the model may declare $W(z):=\kappa/|z|$ with a real coupling $\kappa\in\mathbb R$ (repulsive for $\kappa>0$). Retain a real bounded measurable external term $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b$ as in clause (b)(i), and permit the additional singular term $-g/|x|$, where $g\in\mathbb R$; the total external potential is $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x)-g/|x|$. Thus the declared scalar potential on $\mathbb R^{3N}$ is
$$V(X)=V_b(X)+V_C(X),\qquad V_b(X)=\sum_{i=1}^NV_{\mathrm{ext}}^b(x_i),\qquad V_C(X)=-g\sum_{i=1}^N\frac1{|x_i|}+\kappa\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}\frac1{|x_i-x_j|}.$$
The cases $g=0$, $\kappa=0$, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b=0$ and either sign of either coupling are allowed. Singular values on their null collision sets are irrelevant to the multiplier classes. The singular part is supplied by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]]; the bounded external addition is included by the exact-domain argument in clause (d)(ii), rather than attributed to a source statement which contains only the singular sum.

**(d) The labelled energy operator and its sector restriction.** Fix the
particle masses $m_1=\cdots=m_N=m$ of the declared species.

(i) *Spatial, bounded case.* Put $r_s:=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N:=(\mathbb C^{r_s})^{\otimes N}$ and $M:=r_s^N$. The finite product spin basis identifies $\mathcal S_N$ with $\mathbb C^M$. Use the full finite-component product unitary
$$\Theta_N:H^{\otimes N}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),\qquad [\Theta_N(f_1\otimes\cdots\otimes f_N)]_a(X)=\prod_{j=1}^N[f_j(x_j)]_{a_j},$$
where $a\in\{1,\dots,r_s\}^N$. Its construction and combined spatial/spin permutation action are proved in [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]], from the finite-component extension of [[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]. For $V(X)=\sum_iV_{\mathrm{ext}}(x_i)+\sum_{i<j}W(x_i-x_j)$ define $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\hbar^2\Delta_X/(2m)+M_V$ componentwise. The CC-only [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]], with $a_i=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and component count $M$, supplies self-adjointness on
$$D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C)\otimes \mathcal S_N,$$
and the lower bound $-\|V\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external potentials and the even pair potential make the scalar domain and operator invariant under spatial block permutations. The finite-component lemma shows that the combined permutations $\mathcal U_\pi=\Theta_NU_\pi\Theta_N^{-1}$ also permute the spin slots and commute with $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ on its domain. Thus $\mathcal P_\sigma:=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduces the operator by [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-permutation-restricted-self-adjointness]] (a)-(d), and the transported sector energy is
$$H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}\big|_{D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma}.$$
It is self-adjoint on $\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_N\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the zero operator on the zero-sector branch. The model's tensor reading is $H_N^\sigma:=\Theta_N^{-1}H_N^{\sigma,\mathrm{coord}}\Theta_N$ on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$. Every constant spin action commutes with the spin-independent labelled operator; a common spin unitary $A^{\otimes N}$ preserves each identical-particle sector by the finite-component lemma. For $s=0$, $M=1$ and this is the scalar product reading; for $N=1$, $M=2s+1$ and it is the one-particle component reading.

(ii) *Spatial Coulomb case.* Put $r=2s+1$, $\mathcal S_N=(\mathbb C^r)^{\otimes N}$ and $M=r^N$. Use the full spin-product unitary $\Theta_N:(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^r))^{\otimes N}\to L^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M)$ of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (a),(b), including its combined spatial/internal permutation action. To apply the literal Fourier normalization of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]], choose in that mathematical theorem the masses $\widetilde m_i=m/(4\pi^2)$, its parameter $\hbar$ unchanged, one fixed center at zero, coefficients $z_{i1}=-g$ and $z_{ij}=\kappa$. The mathematical masses here are substitution parameters used to realize the already declared kinetic operator; the physical species mass remains $m$. The source kinetic symbol becomes $4\pi^2\hbar^2|\xi|^2/(2m)$, so its scalar operator is exactly
$$T_C=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C(X),\qquad D(T_C)=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C).$$
By the source's clauses (b),(c), $T_C$ and its finite-component extension are self-adjoint on these exact domains and bounded below for all stated real $g,\kappa$. The real bounded multiplier $M_{V_b}$ has norm at most $N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$, hence relative bound zero with respect to $T_C$ and to its finite-component extension. The canonical [[thm-kato-rellich]] makes
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=-\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}\Delta_X+V_C+V_b,\qquad D(H_{\mathrm{lab}})=H^2(\mathbb R^{3N};\mathbb C^M),$$
self-adjoint on exactly this domain and bounded below; if the singular operator has lower bound $c_C$, the sum has lower bound $c_C-N\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}^b\|_\infty$. Equal masses, identical external slots and pair-independent signed coefficient $\kappa$ make the scalar operator invariant under spatial permutations. These permutations preserve $H^2$ by permuting the weak-derivative coordinates; the constant internal tensor permutations preserve the finite-component domain too. Consequently the combined projections $\mathcal P_\sigma=\Theta_NP_\sigma^{(N)}\Theta_N^{-1}$ reduce $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, and [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] (c) gives self-adjointness of its restriction on the exact domain $H^2\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_\sigma$. The declared sector energy is this restriction transported back by $\Theta_N^{-1}$ to $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$, with the unique zero-space operator when that sector is zero. The AC assumption remains confined to this Coulomb realization as in clause (a).

(iii) *Finite-mode case.* On $K^{\otimes N}$ put
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}:=\sum_{i=1}^N h^{(i)}+\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W^{(ij)},$$
where $h^{(i)}$ is the slot operator of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]] (the identity on all factors but
the $i$-th, $h$ on the $i$-th) and $W^{(ij)}$ is the transport of
$W\in\mathcal B(K\widehat\otimes K)$ to the pair of slots $(i,j)$ by any
permutation moving that pair to the first two slots; the symmetry
$U_{(12)}WU_{(12)}=W$ makes the order of the pair immaterial and
$W\otimes I$ commutes with permutations fixing the first two slots, so the
transported operator is independent of the permutation chosen. Then
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and self-adjoint,
it commutes with every permutation unitary, and the model's sector energy
operator is $H_N^\sigma:=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$.

**(e) The model's energy reading and evolution.** In every realization the
pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is declared to be the **assigned energy
observable** of the $N$-particle sector in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): its
outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{H_N^\sigma}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$ of that
definition clause (b), and its spectral data are those of the self-adjoint
operator constructed in clause (d). The **model evolution** is the unitary
flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b) with this
generator. The identification of the operator with the energy of a concrete
sample, and the assignment of numerical masses, couplings and potentials to a
laboratory species, are tested identifications with uncertainty under P7;
they are not consequences of P1-P6.

**(f) The non-interacting reading.** The model is called **non-interacting**
when $W=0$ (equivalently $\kappa=0$), so that
$H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$; in the spatial realization this is the
case of the external potential summed over slots of the stated bounded or Coulomb realization.

**(g) Scope.** The declared model is a kinematic and dynamical input of this
pair: it fixes a state space, a sector, an energy operator and an evolution,
and nothing else. It asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van
Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no statement about excited threshold
structure, no thermodynamic limit, no equilibration or thermalization, no
measured energy and no identification of its parameters with a particular
laboratory sample beyond the tested identifications of P7. The finite-mode
realization is an idealization confining the one-particle content to $d$
declared modes; the spatial realization is an idealization of an $N$-particle
non-relativistic sample with the declared external field and pair interaction.

## Remarks

- **Why the sector restriction is legitimate.** In the spatial realizations
  the permutation unitaries preserve the domain $W^{2,2}$ and commute with
  $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$, which is exactly the hypothesis of the
  permutation-restricted self-adjointness theorem; in the finite-mode
  realization the bounded operator $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with the
  $U_\pi$ by construction, and a bounded operator commuting with a projection
  restricts to a self-adjoint operator on its range.
- **Units.** $m$ is in kg, $\hbar$ in J s, $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\|V\|_\infty$
  in J, $W$ in J and $\kappa$ in J m; in the finite-mode realization $h$ and
  $W$ are declared directly in joules. No magnetic coupling, spin-orbit term or
  velocity-dependent interaction is part of this model.

The model is an adopted kinematic-dynamical input of the pair; it asserts no stability of matter, no Hunziker-van Winter-Zhislin threshold statement, no thermodynamic limit, no thermalization and no identification with a laboratory sample, and every interaction constant is an empirical model parameter with uncertainty.

items.title: The declared one-body reduced operator and the one-body readout of a sector preparation
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings.** Adopt the state and composition postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1) and the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
in the state reading of
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]] and the observable reading
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]. Work in the
**finite-mode realization** of a declared species sector of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]:
the one-particle space is a finite-dimensional complex Hilbert space $K$ of
dimension $d\ge1$ with its declared orthonormal modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, and
the $N$-particle sector space is
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}\subseteq K^{\otimes N}$
with the declared sector preparations of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]. Assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) The one-body reduced operator.** Let $\rho$ be a declared sector
preparation, that is, a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
The **one-body reduced preparation** of $\rho$ is the density operator
$\gamma_\rho$ on $K$ of clause (e) of
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] (with $H:=K$, $n:=N$ and
the same sector projections). Explicitly, for the sector inclusion $j$ put $\widetilde\rho=j\rho j^*$ on $K^{\otimes N}$, and for the regrouping unitary $J_N:K^{\otimes N}\to K\widehat\otimes K^{\otimes(N-1)}$ put $\gamma_\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_{K^{\otimes(N-1)}}(J_N\widetilde\rho J_N^{-1})$. Here $K^{\otimes0}=\mathbb C$, so $N=1$ gives $\gamma_\rho=\rho$. A zero sector has no preparation and makes this clause vacuous. By that lemma $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator
on $K$ independent of which factor is traced, and for every
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ the pairings are related by
$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O)\bigr)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr),$$
where $\widetilde\rho$ is the zero extension of $\rho$ and $\Sigma(O)$ is the
sum over the $N$ labelled slots of the slot operator $O^{(i)}$.

**(c) The one-body readout.** For a declared **bounded self-adjoint**
$O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with a declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], the model reads the sector
operator
$$A_O:=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}=P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$$
as an **assigned sharp observable** $(A_O,u_O)$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a): it
is bounded and self-adjoint on the nonzero sector space and its outcome law
in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is the law
$\mu^{A_O}_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{A_O}(B))$ of clause (b) of that
definition. The **one-body readout** of $O$ in $\rho$ is the mean of that law
when it exists.

**(d) Scope.** The reduced preparation $\gamma_\rho$ is a mathematical
partial trace of the sector state; it is not asserted to be the state of any
individual particle, and it does not determine the sector preparation $\rho$:
many sector preparations have the same one-body reduction. The definition
asserts no separability or factorization of $\rho$, no result for the spatial
(infinite-dimensional) realization, whose reduction would require the
separable partial trace, and no measurement of individual particle labels,
which are mathematical factor labels by P6 clause (i). Whether a declared
laboratory preparation realizes a sector preparation $\rho$ and a quantity
realizes the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ are tested identifications with uncertainty
under P7, not consequences of this definition.

## Remarks

- **Normalization.** The one-body reduced preparation is normalized as a
  probability state, $\operatorname{tr}\gamma_\rho=1$, while the mean of the
  sum $A_O$ carries the factor $N$; the sum $\Sigma(O)$ is a many-body
  quantity, not a single-particle quantity, and its mean is $N$ times the
  single-particle pairing with $\gamma_\rho$.
- **Choice of retained factor.** Lemma clause (e) shows that reducing over
  any $N-1$ of the labelled factors gives the same operator on $K$; this is
  the precise sense in which the reduction is label independent inside the
  model.
