F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.2 pp. 8-10: single-particle operators (46)-(48) as sums of slot operators in the occupation-number representation

items.physical_scope: The declared one-body reduction of a sector preparation in the framework's finite-mode realization: the reduced preparation on the one-particle mode space, the sector operator that sums a declared bounded one-particle quantity over the labels, and the reading of that sum as an assigned sharp observable. The reduction is a mathematical partial trace of a sector state; it asserts no physical single-particle state, no separability of the sector preparation, no measurement of an individual particle and no fact about a laboratory sample.

items.title: Entropy, the Boltzmann constant and the free-energy functional of the declared finite-sector model
items.statement:
## Definition

**(a) Adopted readings and restricted sector class.** Adopt the observable and
probability postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2)
and the autonomous-dynamics postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] (P4), in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], for the declared
fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]. This definition
applies to the class of declared models whose sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is **finite-dimensional**, in particular to every
finite-mode realization
([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-orbital-occupation-model]]), where
$D:=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ is finite (and may be zero) by
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a),
(b). Write $\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$ for the set of declared sector
preparations, that is, the density operators on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$
([[lem-nrqm-composites-density-and-scalar-spectral-probability]] clause (a)).
If $D=0$, the only operator has trace zero, so
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)=\varnothing$. The partition trace is
$Z_N=0$, and there is no normalized canonical density or equilibrium free
energy; $\log D$, $D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$ and $\log Z_N$ are not used in this
branch. Clauses (b), (d) and (e) below apply when $D\ge1$; the assigned
parameters of (c) can still be declared when $D=0$.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

**(b) Dimensionless entropy.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$
with eigenvalues $w_1,\dots,w_D\ge0$ (counted with multiplicity, in any
order), the **entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$s(\rho):=-\sum_{i:\,w_i>0}w_i\log w_i\in[0,\log D],$$
the quantity of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]]
clause (a) with $\log$ the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]). It is dimensionless, is a function of the
eigenvalue multiset of $\rho$ alone, and equals zero exactly for pure
preparations; by clause (c) of the cited theorem $s(\rho)=\log D$ holds
exactly when $\rho=D^{-1}\mathrm{id}$.

**(c) Boltzmann constant, temperature and inverse temperature.** The model
assigns a positive **Boltzmann constant** $k_B$ and a positive **temperature**
$T$; in the SI conventions of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] the unit of $k_B$ is
$\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$, the unit of $T$ is the kelvin, and
$$k_B=1.380\,649\times10^{-23}\ \mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$$
fixed exactly by the BIPM SI definition. The model declares the **inverse
temperature** $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$, a positive real number in $\mathrm J^{-1}$.
The value and exactness of $k_B$ are unit-convention facts; the assignment of
the parameter $T$ to a physical sample, and the identification of
$\beta=1/(k_BT)$ with an inverse thermodynamic temperature, are adopted
assumptions of the ensemble model of this pair, not consequences of P1-P4,
and are tested identifications with uncertainty under the preparation and
apparatus postulate P7.

**(d) Physical entropy.** The **physical entropy** of $\rho$ is
$$S(\rho):=k_B\,s(\rho),$$
read in $\mathrm J\,\mathrm K^{-1}$. It is nonnegative, is at most
$k_B\log D$, and vanishes exactly for pure preparations.

**(e) Free-energy functional.** For $\rho\in\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$,
let $\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)\in\mathbb R$ be the mean of the
declared energy observable in $\rho$ (finite because $D<\infty$, in the
moment reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).
The **Helmholtz free-energy reading** of $\rho$ is
$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$
read in joules; it is the quantity
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho H)-\beta^{-1}s(\rho)$ of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] clause (a)
at the identified $\beta$. For the canonical operator
$\rho_\beta:=e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}/Z_N$ and
$Z_N:=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}\in(0,\infty)$ (positive finite sum in the
nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(f) Scope.** This definition covers only declared models with
finite-dimensional sector space, with the zero-sector branch of (a), and preparations in
$\mathcal D(\mathfrak H_N^\sigma)$. For a declared spatial realization, whose
sector space is infinite-dimensional, the operator $\rho\log\rho$ need not be
trace class; no entropy, physical entropy or free energy is defined here for
that case, and a separate trace-class statement would be required. The
definition asserts no increase of entropy in time, no equilibration to
$\rho_\beta$, no thermodynamic limit, no pressure or volume variable, and no
measured temperature, entropy or free energy.

## Remarks

- **Why the finite case first.** In the finite-dimensional sector the entropy
  is an ordinary finite sum over $D$ eigenvalues, and the comparison theorem
  of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]] is
  available without any trace-class convergence hypothesis on
  $\rho\log\rho$. The infinite-dimensional questions are deferred rather than
  assumed.
- **Units of $\beta$.** $\beta=1/(k_BT)$ has the unit
  $\mathrm J^{-1}\mathrm K\,\mathrm K^{-1}=\mathrm J^{-1}$, so the exponent
  $\beta H_N^\sigma$ is dimensionless, as the spectral calculus requires.

references.title: BIPM, The International System of Units (SI), 9th edition 2019, Section 2.2 Table 1 printed pages 123-124 (PDF pages 12-13): the Boltzmann constant k is fixed to 1.380 649 x 10^-23 J K^-1 as an exact defining constant

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.3.2 printed pages 127-129 (PDF pages 135-137): the Shannon entropy s = -sum p_i ln p_i and its operator form -Tr(rho ln rho); Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the Gibbs distribution, beta = 1/(k_B T), the thermodynamic entropy S = k_B s (6.98) and the Helmholtz free energy F = -k_B T ln Z (6.99)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.3 printed pages 13-14: the von Neumann entropy S = -sum_j lambda_j ln lambda_j; Section 1.1.5 printed page 15: F = -T ln Z and F = E - T S

items.physical_scope: The framework's reading of entropy and free energy for a declared fixed-N model whose sector space is finite-dimensional (the finite-mode realization): the dimensionless von Neumann entropy of a declared preparation, the assigned Boltzmann constant with its exact SI value, an assigned temperature and inverse temperature, the physical entropy in J K^-1 and the Helmholtz free-energy functional in joules. The identification beta = 1/(k_B T) and the constancy of k_B are adopted model and unit-convention assumptions; the definition asserts no increase of entropy, no equilibration, no thermodynamic limit and no measured temperature or entropy.

items.title: The canonical equilibrium-ensemble assumption: the Gibbs preparation of a declared model at assigned temperature
items.statement:
## Postulate

**(a) Adopted readings and framework data.** Adopt the state and composition
postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]] (P1), the observable
and probability postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]] (P2), the
autonomous-dynamics postulate [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]
(P4) and the preparation and apparatus postulate
[[post-nrqm-framework-preparation-and-apparatus]] (P7), together with the
Boltzmann-constant and temperature conventions of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]. Declare one of the
following model readings of the same **adopted Gibbs assignment**:

(i) a fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]], on its sector space,
with Gibbs generator $G:=H_N^\sigma$; or

(ii) a separately declared number-variable mode model, such as a one-mode
bosonic Fock space, a fermionic occupation space, or a declared countable
independent-mode space, with its declared assigned observables and energy
operator $H$. The model declares a self-adjoint Gibbs generator $G$ on that
space: either $G=H$, or a separately supplied self-adjoint realization of the
effective generator $G=H-\mu\mathcal N$, where $\mathcal N$ is the declared
particle-number operator and $\mu\in\mathbb R$ is an assigned chemical
potential in joules. The subtraction is an operator with its supplied domain,
not an assertion that a formal unbounded difference is self-adjoint.

In either reading assume $G$ is bounded below and give its spectral PVM
$E_G$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]],
[[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Let $T>0$ be an assigned temperature in
kelvin and let $\beta:=1/(k_BT)$ in $\mathrm J^{-1}$ with the assigned
Boltzmann constant $k_B$. The Gibbs assignment to either model, and the
chemical-potential identification in (ii), are additional physical
preparation assumptions made here; they are not derived from P1-P4 or from
the fixed-$N$ construction. In (ii) no restriction on the assigned real
$\mu$ is imposed beyond the declared generator and trace existence
conditions; the mode-specific convergence conditions are proved separately.
For reading (ii), $G$ specifies the Gibbs weights. If the assigned autonomous
dynamics is generated by $H$, stationarity of the Gibbs density requires its
separate dynamical or commutation hypotheses; this assignment does not
identify $H-\mu\mathcal N$ with the physical evolution generator.
The physical Helmholtz free-energy vocabulary of the entropy definition
continues to apply only to its stated nonzero finite-sector class and is not
extended to every effective generator by this postulate.
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of
the spectral calculus.

**(b) Existence hypothesis and the Gibbs preparation.** The model assumes
that the **partition trace is strictly positive and finite**:
$$0<Z:=\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta G}<\infty,$$
where $\operatorname{Tr}B:=\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\langle Bf,f\rangle$ for a
bounded positive $B$ and an orthonormal basis $\mathcal B$, with value allowed
to be $+\infty$. Such a basis exists under the declared AC by the maximal
orthonormal-family argument using [[thm-zorn]] and the zero-complement
criterion of [[thm-parseval-equivalences-for-a-complete-orthonormal-family]].
This trace is basis independent: for $C:=B^{1/2}$ of
[[thm-positive-square-root]], the defining sum is
$\sum_{f\in\mathcal B}\|Cf\|^2$, whose invariance is
[[thm-hilbert-schmidt-norm-is-basis-independent]]. When the sum is finite,
$C$ is Hilbert-Schmidt ([[def-hilbert-schmidt-operator]]), so $B=C^2$ is
trace class by [[thm-trace-class-iff-product-of-two-hilbert-schmidt-operators]],
and its ordinary trace is this same diagonal sum by
[[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]. Apply this to the bounded positive operator $e^{-\beta G}$, since the
declared Gibbs generator $G$ is bounded below. The model
adopts as the **canonical** or **Gibbs preparation** of the declared model
at temperature $T$ the density operator
$$\rho_\beta:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta G}.$$
If the sector is zero-dimensional, its partition trace is $Z=0$, no
trace-one density exists, and no canonical density or equilibrium free
energy is assigned. On a nonzero finite-dimensional model space, $Z$ is a
positive finite sum $\sum_je^{-\beta E_j}$ over the eigenvalues of $G$; no energy
sign restriction is needed. There $\rho_\beta$ is the canonical operator of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-finite-gibbs-free-energy-minimum]], and the
strict positivity and finiteness hypothesis is automatic. In reading (i),
$Z=Z_N$ and this is precisely the finite-sector Gibbs assignment.

Outside the finite-dimensional class the existence hypothesis is a genuine
restriction. For a declared non-interacting fixed-$N$ model with a supplied
countably infinite orthonormal eigenmode basis and real mode energies
$\varepsilon_j$ bounded below, the complete construction and trace criterion
of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-fixed-n-countable-mode-partition-criterion]] give
$Z_N=h_N(q)$ for bosonic statistics or $Z_N=e_N(q)$ for fermionic statistics,
where $q_j=e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j}$ and $h_N,e_N$ are the corresponding
nonnegative occupation-series sums. For every fixed $N\ge1$, either trace is
finite exactly when $\sum_jq_j<\infty$. This is a trace on the fixed-$N$
sector and permits negative mode energies.

For the separately declared full bosonic Fock models of reading (ii),
the single-mode calculation of
[[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] and the product
criterion of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-countable-mode-product-criterion]]
provide the separate mathematical full-Fock traces, with their original
positive mode-energy hypotheses: they sum over every particle number,
including the vacuum, giving $(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon})^{-1}$ for one mode
and $\prod_j(1-e^{-\beta\varepsilon_j})^{-1}$ for countably many modes.
Their physical Gibbs reading is the additional assignment of (a)(ii), not a
consequence of a mathematical trace formula. Those full-Fock traces are not
substituted for the fixed-$N$ partition trace of reading (i).

**(c) The equilibrium assumption and thermal means.** The model **assumes**
that, for a declared sample of the species at the assigned temperature $T$
and in the absence of further preparation information, the preparation
description of the sample is $\rho_\beta$ in the sense of P1. For an assigned
sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ with spectral PVM $E_A$, define its outcome law
$\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta E_A(B))$ as in
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b).
If and only if the absolute first moment is finite,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}|a|\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a)<\infty,$$
the model defines the **thermal mean** at temperature $T$ by
$$\langle A\rangle_\beta:=\int_{\mathbb R}a\,d\mu_{\rho_\beta}^A(a),$$
read in the assigned unit $u_A$. For bounded $A$ this equals
$\operatorname{tr}(\rho_\beta A)=\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$. For
unbounded $A$, if the mean exists and the literal product $A\rho_\beta$ is
defined on the whole Hilbert space and is trace class, the mean also equals
$\operatorname{tr}(A\rho_\beta)$ and
$\operatorname{tr}(\overline{\rho_\beta A})$; these conditional product
identities are proved by the density eigenexpansion in
[[lem-nrqm-many-body-spectral-mean-and-defined-trace-product]]. First-moment
existence alone imposes no such product or operator-square-domain condition.
When the absolute first moment is infinite the model asserts no finite
thermal mean. The identification of the parameter $T$ with the thermodynamic temperature of a
sample, and of $\beta$ with its inverse temperature, is part of this
assumption; the stated conservation and equilibrium properties of
$\rho_\beta$ under the flow of P4, and the extremal property of $\rho_\beta$
among preparations, are separate conditional results of this pair.

**(d) Motivation and status.** The assumption is motivated, but not
established, by the maximum-entropy reasoning of the cited sources: among
preparations with a prescribed mean energy, the Gibbs weights maximize the
entropy functional, and the finite-dimensional comparison theorem makes
$\rho_\beta$ the minimizer of the corresponding functional built from $G$.
Its physical Helmholtz free-energy reading applies in the stated finite
fixed-sector class; an effective-generator interpretation in a different
mode model is a separate declared reading. That reasoning is
an argument inside mathematical statistics and thermodynamics; it does not
derive the physical assumption that a sample is described by $\rho_\beta$.
The postulate is an **adopted** statistical-mechanical assumption of the
model, in the sense of the content model's distinction between adopted
assumptions and derived consequences.

**(e) Scope.** The postulate asserts nothing about how a sample reaches the
Gibbs preparation; in particular it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration
time, no ergodicity, no master-equation or Markov approximation, no
thermodynamic limit, no pressure, volume or phase-transition structure, and
no measured temperature or expectation. The requirement $0<Z<\infty$ is part
of the assumption; the model does not define a canonical preparation when
$Z=0$ or the partition trace diverges. Any comparison with a laboratory sample requires the
declared preparation, isolation, detection and sampling models of P7, and
agreement of a thermal prediction with data is evidence about the combined
model and apparatus assumptions, not a proof of the framework or of this
postulate.

## Remarks

- **The finite-sector case.** For a nonzero finite-dimensional sector the existence
  hypothesis is a positive finite sum and hence automatic (and likewise for
  any separately declared nonzero finite-dimensional mode space); the only content of clause
  (b) there is the assignment of the Gibbs weights to the declared energies.
- **Relation to P4.** The postulate adds a preparation assumption to the
  dynamics; by itself P4 describes the unitary evolution of whatever
  preparation is declared, and does not single out $\rho_\beta$. The precise
  sense in which unitary evolution cannot produce $\rho_\beta$ from a
  different preparation is a separate theorem of this pair.

references.title: J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.4 printed pages 129-131 (PDF pages 137-139): the maximum-entropy motivation, the Gibbs distribution rho = Z^{-1} sum e^{-beta E_i}|i><i| (6.94), beta = 1/(k_B T) and Z = sum e^{-beta E_i} (6.93a,b), U = Tr(H rho) (6.95) and S = k_B s (6.98)

I. Burmistrov and A. Lunkin, Lecture Notes on Statistical Mechanics (HSE, January 10, 2023), Section 1.1.2 printed page 13: the Gibbs distribution rho = e^{-beta H}/Z, Z = Tr e^{-beta H}, with beta a formal inverse-energy parameter; Section 1.1.4 printed pages 14-15: the maximal-entropy principle and the free energy F = -T ln Z

items.physical_scope: The adopted equilibrium-ensemble assumption of the many-body pair: for a declared fixed-N model or a separately declared number-variable mode model with self-adjoint semibounded Gibbs generator G (including a declared effective generator H-mu N), assigned temperature and strictly positive finite partition trace, the Gibbs preparation rho_beta = e^{-beta G}/Z, its thermal means, and the identifications of beta = 1/(k_B T) and of rho_beta with the model's description of thermal equilibrium. It is an adopted statistical-mechanical assumption motivated by maximum-entropy reasoning, not a consequence of the framework's state, probability or dynamics postulates; it asserts no thermalization, no equilibration rate, no thermodynamic limit and no fact about a laboratory sample except through the tested identifications of P7.

items.title: Diagonalisation of the non-interacting finite-mode sector: occupation eigenvalues, partition sum and ground energy
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4
([[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]]) and the identical-particle and
spin postulate P6 ([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in
the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Work in the
finite-mode realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]]: one-particle space
$K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with declared modes $(f_1,\dots,f_d)$,
particle number $N\ge1$, sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, one-particle
self-adjoint operator $h\in\mathcal B(K)$, and **non-interacting** interaction
$W=0$, so that $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_{i=1}^Nh^{(i)}$ and
$H_N^\sigma=H_{\mathrm{lab}}|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ in the notation of that
definition. Let $e_1,\dots,e_d$ be an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of
$h$ with real eigenvalues $\varepsilon_1,\dots,\varepsilon_d$ and let
$\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\cdots\le\varepsilon_{(d)}$ be the nondecreasing
rearrangement of the list. Then:

(a) *the labelled operator is diagonal*: $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is bounded and
self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$, it commutes with every
permutation unitary $U_\pi$, and for every multi-index
$i=(i_1,\dots,i_N)\in\{1,\dots,d\}^N$,
$$H_{\mathrm{lab}}\,(e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N})=\Bigl(\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{i_k}\Bigr)e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N};$$

(b) *occupation eigenvalues and spectrum*: for every $N$-element subset
$J\subseteq\{1,\dots,d\}$ the Slater vector $e_J^\wedge$ of
[[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b) is an
eigenvector of $H_N^-$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_J:=\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j$,
and for every occupation vector $\lambda\in W(N,d)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb N^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$
the symmetric vector $m_\lambda$ of clause (c) is an eigenvector of
$H_N^+$ with eigenvalue $\lambda_\lambda:=\sum_{j=1}^d\lambda_j\varepsilon_j$;
the families $(e_J^\wedge)$ and $(m_\lambda)$ are orthogonal bases of
$\mathfrak H_N^-$ and $\mathfrak H_N^+$ respectively, so the spectrum of
$H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of these eigenvalues (with multiplicities
given by the number of configurations producing them); for $\sigma=-$ and
$N>d$ the sector space is $\{0\}$ and the model has no sector states;

(c) *partition sum and ground energy*: write
$$\mathcal C_N^\sigma:=\{\lambda\in W(N,d):\lambda_j\le1\ \text{for every }j\ \text{if }\sigma=-\},\qquad M_N^\sigma:=|\mathcal C_N^\sigma|=\dim\mathfrak H_N^\sigma.$$
The configuration counts are $M_N^- =\binom dN$ and
$M_N^+ =\binom{N+d-1}{N}$. For every $\beta>0$,
$$Z_N(\beta):=\operatorname{tr}e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$$
is finite. If $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$, then $\mathcal C_N^-=\varnothing$,
$Z_N(\beta)=0$, and there is no ground eigenvalue or trace-one density
operator on the zero sector; in particular no normalized Gibbs density can
be formed there. Otherwise $M_N^\sigma>0$ and $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$.
In this nonzero-sector case, let
$$E_0:=\min_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda,\qquad E_{\max}:=\max_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}\lambda_\lambda.$$
Then the actual Boltzmann bounds are
$$M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le Z_N(\beta)\le M_N^\sigma e^{-\beta E_0}.$$
No nonnegativity hypothesis on the $\varepsilon_j$ is imposed. For
$\sigma=-$ and $N\le d$,
$$E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)},\qquad E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)},$$
and for $\sigma=+$,
$$E_0=N\varepsilon_{(1)},\qquad E_{\max}=N\varepsilon_{(d)}.$$
For every unit vector $\psi\in\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ in either nonzero sector,
$\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle\ge E_0$, with equality exactly on the
eigenspace of $E_0$;

(d) *reading and stationarity*: on a nonzero sector the pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the
model's assigned energy observable; in a declared sector preparation $\rho$
its outcome law is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$,
and in the pure preparation of each sector basis vector of clause (b) this
law is the point mass at the displayed eigenvalue; each such vector is a
stationary state of the model evolution $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$, and
the energy law of every declared sector preparation is the law of the finite
spectral sum in the sector basis;

(e) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the finite-mode idealization, on
the declared $h$ and on $W=0$; it asserts nothing for interacting models, for
spatial realizations, for infinite mode families, about thermal states or
equilibration, and about any laboratory system.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-mode non-interacting model data of the statement with its eigenbasis $(e_1,\dots,e_d)$, eigenvalues $\varepsilon_j$, sector projections $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and sector space $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$.

[F1] **Finite spectral theorem.** A self-adjoint endomorphism $h$ of the finite-dimensional complex inner product space $K$ is normal, so $K$ has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors of $h$ with real eigenvalues ([[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], [[def-hilbert-space]]).

[F2] **Slot operators.** For $h\in\mathcal B(K)$ the slot operator $h^{(i)}$ acts on elementary tensors by $h^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes hv_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|h^{(i)}\|\le\|h\|$, and $(h^{(i)})^*=(h^*)^{(i)}$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], [[def-operator-norm]]).

[F3] **Product basis and occupation bases.** The elementary tensors $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ over all multi-indices form an orthonormal basis of $K^{\otimes N}$; the Slater vectors $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}(e_{j_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{j_N})$ over $N$-element subsets $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ form an orthonormal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_-^{(N)}$ with $e_J^\wedge$ zero-free for distinct indices and vanishing on repeated indices; the vectors $m_\lambda=\sum_{c\in\operatorname{orb}(\lambda)}e_c$ over $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ form an orthogonal basis of $\operatorname{ran}P_+^{(N)}$, and $N_je_J^\wedge=\mathbf 1_J(j)e_J^\wedge$, $N_jm_\lambda=\lambda_jm_\lambda$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clauses (a), (b), (c), (d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]], [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F4] **Configuration counts.** The map $J\mapsto\mathbf 1_J$ is a bijection from $N$-element subsets onto $\{\lambda\in\{0,1\}^d:\sum_j\lambda_j=N\}$, the sector dimensions are $\binom dN$ and $\binom{N+d-1}{N}$, and for $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is $\{0\}$ ([[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-finite-mode-occupation-counts]] clauses (a), (b), (c), [[thm-nrqm-identical-particles-occupation-number-basis]] clause (b)).

[F5] **Stationary states.** For the assigned energy observable $(H_{\mathrm{op}},u_H)$ with flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_{\mathrm{op}}/\hbar)$, a nonzero $\psi$ is an eigenvector of $H_{\mathrm{op}}$ if and only if its pure preparation is stationary, and then $\psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\psi$ ([[pthm-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-stationary-states-and-energy-conservation]] clause (c)); the outcome law of an assigned observable in a preparation is the trace law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b), and the trace is basis independent ([[thm-trace-is-absolutely-convergent-and-basis-independent]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; expand in the product basis of one-particle eigenmodes, transport the diagonal action to the two sector bases, and read the finite spectrum and trace.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The labelled operator on the product basis] By [F2] each $h^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}=\sum_ih^{(i)}$ is bounded and self-adjoint with $\|H_{\mathrm{lab}}\|\le N\|h\|$. On the product basis vector $e_i=e_{i_1}\otimes\cdots\otimes e_{i_N}$ the $i$-th slot operator acts as $h$ on the factor $e_{i_k}$, giving $h^{(k)}e_i=\varepsilon_{i_k}e_i$; hence $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_k\varepsilon_{i_k})e_i$. Since every $U_\pi$ permutes the slots and $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ is the sum over all slots, $U_\pi H_{\mathrm{lab}}U_\pi^*=H_{\mathrm{lab}}$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 [Sector eigenvectors] Let $J=\{j_1<\cdots<j_N\}$ and $i=(j_1,\dots,j_N)$. By [F3], $e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i$; since $H_{\mathrm{lab}}$ commutes with $P_-^{(N)}$ by step 1.1 and [F3], $H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_J^\wedge=\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}H_{\mathrm{lab}}e_i=(\sum_{j\in J}\varepsilon_j)\sqrt{N!}P_-^{(N)}e_i=\lambda_Je_J^\wedge$. Likewise, for $\lambda\in W(N,d)$ and any multi-index $c$ with $|c|=\lambda$ one has $P_+^{(N)}e_c=\gamma_cm_\lambda$ with $\gamma_c>0$ by [F3], so $H_{\mathrm{lab}}m_\lambda=(\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j)m_\lambda$; because the $e_J^\wedge$ and the $m_\lambda$ are orthogonal bases of the respective sectors by [F3], [F4], the spectrum of $H_N^\sigma$ is the finite set of the displayed eigenvalues with the configurations as multiplicities, and for $\sigma=-$, $N>d$ the sector is $\{0\}$. This proves (b). [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Partition sum and the zero sector] Normalize the symmetric vectors to $\widetilde m_\lambda:=m_\lambda/\|m_\lambda\|$; by [F3] these form an orthonormal eigenbasis, as do the Slater vectors in the fermionic sector. The trace is therefore $Z_N(\beta)=\sum_{\lambda\in\mathcal C_N^\sigma}e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}$, with the configuration counts $M_N^-=\binom dN$ and $M_N^+=\binom{N+d-1}{N}$ from [F4]. For $\sigma=-$, $N>d$, the index set is empty and the trace is the empty sum $0$. There is no eigenvector on $\{0\}$ and hence no ground eigenvalue, and its only operator has trace $0$, so no trace-one density or normalized Gibbs density exists there. In every other case [F4] gives a finite nonempty index set, so its finite sum of positive Boltzmann weights has $0<Z_N(\beta)<\infty$. For that case finite minima and maxima $E_0,E_{\max}$ exist, and for each configuration $e^{-\beta E_{\max}}\le e^{-\beta\lambda_\lambda}\le e^{-\beta E_0}$, because $\beta>0$; summing the $M_N^\sigma$ inequalities proves the two bounds. This argument allows negative configuration energies. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 [Reading and stationarity] The pair $(H_N^\sigma,\mathrm J)$ is the model's assigned energy observable of clause (e) of the declared-model definition, so by [F5] its outcome law in a declared sector preparation $\rho$ is $\mu_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_{H_N^\sigma}(B))$; for the pure preparation of a sector basis vector $\Psi$ of step 2.1, $E(\{\lambda\})\Psi=\Psi$ and hence $\mu_\Psi$ is the point mass at $\lambda$. By [F5] and step 2.1 each such $\Psi$ is an eigenvector of the generator, so its pure preparation is stationary under the flow $U(t)=\exp(-itH_N^\sigma/\hbar)$ with $\Psi(t)=e^{-it\lambda/\hbar}\Psi$, and the energy law of any preparation is the finite spectral law in the sector basis. This proves (d). [F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Extreme energies and ground eigenspace] Work on a nonzero sector. For $\sigma=-$, each configuration selects $N$ distinct eigenvalues, so its energy is at least the sum of the $N$ smallest and at most the sum of the $N$ largest; these bounds are attained by the corresponding subsets. Thus $E_0=\sum_{k=1}^N\varepsilon_{(k)}$ and $E_{\max}=\sum_{k=d-N+1}^d\varepsilon_{(k)}$. A minimizing subset contains every mode with energy strictly below $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, contains no mode with energy strictly above $\varepsilon_{(N)}$, and fills its remaining places with modes at that boundary energy; this includes all choices allowed by degeneracy. For $\sigma=+$, the identity $\sum_j\lambda_j=N$ gives $N\varepsilon_{(1)}\le\sum_j\lambda_j\varepsilon_j\le N\varepsilon_{(d)}$; the two bounds are attained by putting all particles in a minimum-energy or maximum-energy mode respectively. Equality at the lower bound holds exactly when every occupied mode has energy $\varepsilon_{(1)}$. Finally expand a unit vector in the orthonormal sector basis of step 3.1: $\psi=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$, $\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2=1$. Then $\langle H_N^\sigma\psi,\psi\rangle-E_0=\sum_\lambda|c_\lambda|^2(\lambda_\lambda-E_0)\ge0$, with equality exactly when all coefficients at energies greater than $E_0$ vanish, that is, exactly on the ground eigenspace. Together with step 3.1 this proves (c). [F3, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1 and 2.1 prove (a) and (b), steps 3.1 and 4.1 prove (c) and step 3.2 proves (d). The argument used the finite-mode idealization, the declared non-interacting $h$ and the finite-dimensional spectral and tensor calculus; no interaction, spatial realization, infinite mode family, thermal state, equilibration or laboratory identification entered, which is (e). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 3.2] ∎

## Remarks

- **Basis independence.** The eigenvalues $\lambda_J$ and $\lambda_\lambda$ depend on the eigenvalue list of $h$, not on the choice of eigenbasis; a degenerate one-particle eigenvalue contributes with its multiplicity through the distinct configurations.
- **Fermionic emptiness.** For $\sigma=-$ and $N>d$ the antisymmetric sector is zero: the algebraic partition trace is $0$, while there are no sector states, no ground eigenvalue and no normalized density. The observable and stationarity readings of clause (d) apply only to nonzero sectors.
- **Energy reference.** The bounds in (c) permit arbitrary real one-particle energies. If all configuration energies are nonnegative, then $Z_N\le M_N^\sigma$; this count-only upper bound is not valid for unrestricted negative energies. Shifting every one-particle energy by $a\in\mathbb R$ multiplies $Z_N$ by $e^{-\beta Na}$ and shifts both extreme energies by $Na$.

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Sections 1.2-1.3 pp. 5-9: the occupation-number basis and the diagonal form of a non-interacting many-body Hamiltonian in second quantisation

The theorem is conditional on P1, P2, P4 and P6, on the adopted finite-mode idealization and on the declared one-particle Hamiltonian; it asserts no interaction, no spatial or infinite-mode result, no thermal state, no thermodynamic limit and no laboratory identification.

items.title: The one-body readout law: sector means of summed bounded one-particle quantities and their reduced forms
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]])
and the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]]
and [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], and assume
the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]) as the choice hypotheses
of the cited tensor, permutation and trace suppliers. Work in the finite-mode
realization of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-one-body-reduced-operator]]:
one-particle space $K$ of finite dimension $d\ge1$ with modes
$(f_1,\dots,f_d)$, integer $N\ge1$ with nonzero sector space
$\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$, and the slot
operators $O^{(i)}$, sum $\Sigma(O)$ and one-body reduced preparation
$\gamma_\rho$ of that definition. Let $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ be self-adjoint
with declared unit $u_O$ in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. Then:

(a) *the readout is an assigned observable*: the sector operator
$A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is bounded and self-adjoint, so the
pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is an assigned sharp observable of the sector in the sense
of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a);

(b) *the mean law*: for every declared sector preparation $\rho$ the mean of
the outcome law of $(A_O,u_O)$ in $\rho$ exists and equals
$$m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}\bigl(\gamma_\rho\,O\bigr);$$

(c) *product-type preparations*: if $u_1,\dots,u_N\in K$ are pairwise
orthonormal and $\rho=T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ with $\Psi:=S(u_1,\dots,u_N)$ the Slater
vector of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clause (a) for $\sigma=-$, or $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$
for $\sigma=+$ (both unit vectors of the sector), then
$\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$ and
$$m_\rho(A_O)=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle;$$

(d) *scope*: the theorem is conditional on the adopted sector of P6, on the
declared finite-mode idealization and on the declared preparation; it asserts
no measured mean, no property of an individual labelled particle, no
separability of $\rho$, no result for spatial infinite-mode models, and no
sampling or detection model. The equality $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$
is exact within the model.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the finite-mode sector data of the statement, the self-adjoint $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ with unit $u_O$, and a declared sector preparation $\rho$.

[F1] **Sector vocabulary.** $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma=\operatorname{ran}P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is a closed subspace of $K^{\otimes N}$; every permutation unitary $U_\pi$ preserves it and acts there as the scalar $\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\pi)$; a declared sector preparation is a density operator on $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ ([[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]] clauses (c)-(d), [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clause (c)).

[F2] **Slot operators and reduction.** For $O\in\mathcal B(K)$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,N\}$ the slot operator $O^{(i)}$ satisfies $O^{(i)}(v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes Ov_i\otimes\cdots\otimes v_N$, is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, and $(O^{(i)})^*=(O^*)^{(i)}$; $\Sigma(O)=\sum_iO^{(i)}$ commutes with every $U_\pi$ and with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, preserves the sectors, and for every sector preparation $\rho$ with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ one has $\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$, where $\gamma_\rho$ is a density operator on $K$ ([[lem-nrqm-many-body-one-body-reduction-trace-law]] clauses (a), (c), (d), (e)).

[F3] **Observable reading and moments.** An assigned sharp observable $(A,u_A)$ has outcome law $\mu^A_\rho(B)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E_A(B))$; for a bounded self-adjoint $A$ and every preparation $\rho$ the mean exists and equals $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A)$, and for a pure preparation of a unit vector $\psi$ it equals $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (a), (b), [[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clauses (a), (d), [[prop-trace-is-linear]], [[thm-cyclicity-of-the-trace]]).

[F4] **Slater and symmetric product vectors.** For pairwise orthonormal $u_1,\dots,u_N$ the Slater vector $S(u_1,\dots,u_N)=N!^{-1/2}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)u_{\sigma(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes u_{\sigma(N)}$ has norm one and equals $\sqrt{N!}\,P_-^{(N)}(u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N)$ ([[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clauses (a), (b)); setting $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$, orthonormality gives $\langle P_+^{(N)}x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\sum_{\sigma\in S_N}\langle U_\sigma x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}\langle x,x\rangle=\frac1{N!}$, so $\Psi:=\sqrt{N!}\,P_+^{(N)}x$ is a unit vector of the symmetric sector with $P_+^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]] clauses (b), (c), [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]]).

[F5] **Rank-one pairing.** $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ is bounded with $\operatorname{tr}(T_{u,v})=\langle u,v\rangle$ and $T_{u,v}^*=T_{v,u}$; the map $(u,v)\mapsto T_{u,v}$ is linear in $u$ and conjugate-linear in $v$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]] clauses (a), (b), (c)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; read the sector sum as a bounded observable, apply the supplied reduction identity, and evaluate the product-type cases by orthonormality of the mode family.

**Given:** the data of the statement and [F1]-[F5].

1.1 [The readout is a bounded self-adjoint sector observable] By [F2] each slot operator is bounded with $\|O^{(i)}\|\le\|O\|$, so $\Sigma(O)$ is bounded with $\|\Sigma(O)\|\le N\|O\|$; since $O=O^*$, [F2] gives $O^{(i)*}=O^{(i)}$ for every $i$ and $\Sigma(O)^*=\Sigma(O)$. By [F2] $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$, hence preserves $\mathfrak H_N^\sigma$ and its orthogonal complement, and the restriction $A_O=\Sigma(O)|_{\mathfrak H_N^\sigma}$ is a bounded self-adjoint operator on the sector space; with the unit $u_O$ the pair $(A_O,u_O)$ is therefore an assigned sharp observable in the sense of [F3]. [F2, F3, def. bounded, algebra]

1.2 [Reduced preparation of product-type states] Let $u_1,\dots,u_N$ be pairwise orthonormal, put $x:=u_1\otimes\cdots\otimes u_N$ and let $\Psi$ be the unit vector of clause (c) for $\sigma=-$ or $\sigma=+$; both satisfy $P_\sigma^{(N)}\Psi=\Psi$ by [F4], and both equal $\sqrt{N!}\,P_\sigma^{(N)}x$. Since $\Sigma(O)$ commutes with $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ and $P_\sigma^{(N)}$ is self-adjoint, $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=N!\langle\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,P_\sigma^{(N)}x\rangle=N!\langle P_\sigma^{(N)}\Sigma(O)P_\sigma^{(N)}x,x\rangle=N!\cdot\frac1{N!}\sum_{\tau\in S_N}\operatorname{sgn}_\sigma(\tau)\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle$, with $\operatorname{sgn}_+=1$ and $\operatorname{sgn}_-=\operatorname{sgn}$. For fixed $\tau$, $\langle\Sigma(O)U_\tau x,x\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_{\tau^{-1}(i)},u_i\rangle\prod_{k\ne i}\langle u_{\tau^{-1}(k)},u_k\rangle$ by [F1] and the elementary-tensor pairing, and orthonormality makes every factor $\delta_{\tau^{-1}(k),k}$ vanish unless $\tau=\mathrm{id}$; hence only the identity permutation contributes and $\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{i=1}^N\langle Ou_i,u_i\rangle$. [F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 [The mean law] Let $\rho$ be a declared sector preparation with zero extension $\widetilde\rho$ and let $A_O$ be the readout of step 1.1. Since $A_O$ is bounded, [F3] gives $m_\rho(A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)$, and by steps 1.1 and [F2], $\operatorname{tr}(\rho A_O)=\operatorname{tr}(\widetilde\rho\,\Sigma(O))=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. This proves (a) and (b). [F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 [Product-type means and the reduced preparation] In the situation of step 1.2, the mean is $m_\rho(A_O)=\langle\Sigma(O)\Psi,\Psi\rangle=\sum_{j=1}^N\langle Ou_j,u_j\rangle$, while the mean law of step 2.1 gives $m_\rho(A_O)=N\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho O)$. The identity extends from self-adjoint $O$ to every $O$ by writing $O=(O+O^*)/2+i(O-O^*)/(2i)$ and using linearity of both pairings. Testing it against $O=T_{u,v}$ and using [F5], $\operatorname{tr}(\gamma_\rho T_{u,v})=\langle\gamma_\rho u,v\rangle$ and $N^{-1}\sum_j\langle T_{u,v}u_j,u_j\rangle=N^{-1}\sum_j\langle u_j,v\rangle\langle u,u_j\rangle$; the identity for all $u,v$ therefore gives $\gamma_\rho=N^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^NT_{u_j,u_j}$, since two endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional space with equal pairings against every rank-one operator are equal. This proves (c). [F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 [Conclusion and scope] Steps 1.1-2.1 prove (a) and (b) and step 3.1 proves (c). Every quantity is a spectral datum of the declared finite-mode sector model and the argument used only P1, P2, P6 and the finite-dimensional tensor and trace calculus; no measured mean, individual-particle property, separability statement or spatial reduction entered, which is (d). [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Remarks

- **The factor $N$ and the normalization of $\gamma_\rho$.** The reduced preparation is normalized as a probability state on the one-particle space, while $A_O$ sums $N$ slot terms; the product-type case shows the two conventions consistently: a Slater determinant of $N$ orthonormal modes has reduced preparation the equal-weight mixture of those modes.
- **No separability claim.** The mean law holds for arbitrary sector preparations, entangled or not; nothing in the argument factors $\rho$, and the product-type clause is a special case.

Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Sections 6.2-6.3 and 10.1 printed pages 116-126 and 226-230 (PDF pages 124-134 and 234-238): local operators on a composite system, the reduced density operator of one factor, and identical-particle exchange symmetry with the two-particle example

F. H. L. Essler, Advanced Quantum Theory (Oxford lecture notes, 2017/18), Section 1.4.2 pp. 8-10: single-particle operators as sums over particle labels (46)-(48) and their second-quantised form (49)-(52)

items.physical_scope: The conditional one-body readout law of the declared finite-mode many-body model: for a bounded self-adjoint one-particle quantity the summed sector operator is an assigned sharp observable, its mean in every declared sector preparation exists and is N times the pairing of the one-body reduced preparation with the quantity, and for declared Slater and orthonormal-mode symmetric preparations the reduced preparation is the equal-weight mixture of the occupied modes. The theorem is conditional on P1, P2 and P6, the adopted finite-mode idealization and the declared preparation; it asserts no measured mean, no individual-particle property, no separability of the sector state and no spatial (infinite-mode) reduction.

items.title: Direct and exchange contributions to a two-fermion mean energy and the repulsive-Coulomb ordering
items.statement:
## Statement

Adopt the state and composition postulate P1
([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]]), the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]]),
the non-relativistic kinematics postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]) and
the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]) in the readings of
[[def-nrqm-identical-particles-framework-species-sectors-and-preparations]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]], and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Take a declared spin-$\tfrac12$ fermionic species
with mass $m>0$, the spatial realization of the declared fixed-$N$ model of
[[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-declared-fixed-n-model]] with $N=2$, a
bounded real external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and one of the following
two pair interactions: (bounded case) a bounded real even
$W:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R$; (Coulomb case) $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$ with
$\kappa>0$ and $V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ bounded. Let $u,v\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
be pairwise orthonormal spatial orbitals, put
$$\varepsilon_u:=\langle h u,u\rangle_\star,\qquad \varepsilon_v:=\langle h v,v\rangle_\star$$
with $h=-\hbar^2\Delta/(2m)+V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ the declared one-particle operator and $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_\star$
the $L^2(\mathbb R^3)$ pairing, and let $D$ and $X$ be the direct and
exchange integrals
$$D=\int_{\mathbb R^6}|u(x)|^2|v(y)|^2W(x-y)\,dx\,dy,\qquad X=\int_{\mathbb R^6}\overline{u(x)}v(x)u(y)\overline{v(y)}\,W(x-y)\,dx\,dy$$
of [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]]
clauses (c),(d), as appropriate. Fix the standard orthonormal basis $e_\uparrow,e_\downarrow$ of the declared spin-$\tfrac12$ factor $\mathbb C^2$, and define the unit spin vectors
$$\chi_-=(e_\uparrow\otimes e_\downarrow-e_\downarrow\otimes e_\uparrow)/\sqrt2,\qquad \chi_+=(e_\uparrow\otimes e_\downarrow+e_\downarrow\otimes e_\uparrow)/\sqrt2,$$
read as the singlet and symmetric $S_z=0$ triplet of the declared basis. Let $\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}$ be the scalar Euclidean product unitary and let
$$\Theta_2:(L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^2))^{\otimes2}\longrightarrow L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^2\otimes\mathbb C^2)$$
be the full spin-product unitary of [[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] clause (a). Put
$$\varphi_\pm=(u\otimes v\pm v\otimes u)/\sqrt2,\qquad f_\pm=\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}\varphi_\pm,\qquad \Phi_\pm=\Theta_2^{-1}(f_\pm\chi_\mp),\qquad \rho_\pm=T_{\Phi_\pm,\Phi_\pm}.$$
Thus $\Phi_\pm$ are vectors in the declared one-particle tensor square, not untransported vectors in a regrouped spatial/spin product. They define the two declared preparations after the sector membership proved below. No reality assumption is imposed on the complex orbitals $u,v$.

(a) *declared preparations*: $\Phi_\pm$ are unit vectors of the antisymmetric
sector $\mathfrak H_2^-$ of the model, and $\rho_\pm$ are declared sector
preparations;

(b) *mean energies*: the means of the declared energy observable in the two
preparations exist, are finite and equal
$$m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D+X,\qquad m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D-X;$$
in particular the **exchange splitting** of the two preparations is
$m_{\rho_+}-m_{\rho_-}=2X$;

(c) *repulsive-Coulomb ordering*: in the Coulomb case with $u,v\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$
one has $X\ge0$ and therefore $m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)\le m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)$: the
spatially antisymmetric, spin-triplet preparation has the lower mean pair
energy of the two;

(d) *scope*: clauses (a)-(c) are conditional consequences of the declared
model, the declared orbitals and the adopted spin-statistics sector of P6;
they derive no spin-statistics theorem, assert no measured energy difference,
compare no experimental spectrum, and make no claim that the declared
orbitals approximate any atomic state.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the declared spin-1/2 fermionic species, $N=2$, the external and pair data of the statement, the orthonormal orbitals $u,v\in W^{2,2}$, the spin vectors $\chi_\pm$ and the vectors $\Phi_\pm$.

[F1] **Full spin-product transport.** The unitary $\Theta_2$ maps $(f e_a)\otimes(g e_b)$ to $(x,y)\mapsto f(x)g(y)(e_a\otimes e_b)$. The transported exchange acts as $(\mathcal U\Psi)(x,y)=R\Psi(y,x)$, where $R(\zeta\otimes\eta)=\eta\otimes\zeta$ swaps the two spin factors; its antisymmetric projection is $\mathcal P_-=(I-\mathcal U)/2=\Theta_2P_-^{(2)}\Theta_2^{-1}$. Finite spin components preserve the $H^2$ domain, and a permutation-invariant scalar self-adjoint operator with that domain restricts self-adjointly to this combined sector ([[lem-nrqm-many-body-finite-spin-product-identification]] clauses (a)–(c)). Tensor pairings and norms are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], and the tensor exchange is that of [[lem-nrqm-composites-permutation-sector-projections]].

[F2] **Scalar spatial products.** The scalar product unitary $\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}$ has $\Theta_{\mathrm{sp}}(u\otimes v)(x,y)=u(x)v(y)$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-euclidean-l2-product-unitary]]). Fubini applies to integrable products and the finite component pairings ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

[F3] **Direct and exchange integrals, including complex orbitals.** For a real bounded even $W$, the displayed $D,X$ converge absolutely, are real and satisfy $\langle M_Wf_\pm,f_\pm\rangle=D\pm X$ for arbitrary complex orthonormal $u,v\in L^2$. For $W(z)=\kappa/|z|$, $\kappa>0$, the same assertion holds for arbitrary complex orthonormal $u,v\in H^1$, with $f_\pm\in D(M_W)$, $D\ge0$ and $X\ge0$. These are [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-slater-direct-and-exchange-calculation]] clauses (c),(d); its proof 2.1 proves Coulomb positivity with only the $L^1$ overlap density, without an unclaimed $L^2$ or real-orbital hypothesis.

[F4] **The exact labelled realization with bounded external addition.** Put $a=\hbar^2/(2m)$ and $V_b(x,y)=V_{\mathrm{ext}}(x)+V_{\mathrm{ext}}(y)$. In the bounded case the scalar labelled operator $T=-a\Delta_{(x,y)}+V_b+W(x-y)$ is self-adjoint on $H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C)$ by [[lem-nrqm-many-body-cc-bounded-spatial-realization]], with the same finite-component realization on $H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$. In the Coulomb case apply [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-fixed-n-coulomb-self-adjointness]] clauses (b),(c) with mathematical masses $\widetilde m_1=\widetilde m_2=m/(4\pi^2)$, its parameter $\hbar$ unchanged, zero external singular coefficients and pair coefficient $\kappa$. Its kinetic Fourier symbol is then $4\pi^2a(|\xi|^2+|\eta|^2)$, exactly the physical $-a\Delta_{(x,y)}$, so $T_C=-a\Delta_{(x,y)}+\kappa/|x-y|$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$. The multiplier $M_{V_b}$ is bounded self-adjoint, with norm at most $2\|V_{\mathrm{ext}}\|_\infty$ and relative bound zero with respect to $T_C$; [[thm-kato-rellich]] therefore makes $T=T_C+M_{V_b}$ self-adjoint on the same exact domain and bounded below. In either case, $T$ preserves the spatial exchange symmetry because its Laplacian and real even pair kernel and identical external slots are exchange invariant. The full labelled operator $T_4$ acts componentwise on spin and its combined antisymmetric restriction, transported by $\Theta_2^{-1}$, is the declared $H_2^-$ with exact domain $\Theta_2^{-1}(H^2\cap\operatorname{ran}\mathcal P_-)$ by [F1]. No scalar-only application of a permutation theorem is used for the spin-four space. The one-particle $h=-a\Delta+V_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is likewise self-adjoint on scalar $H^2$ by the CC bounded realization.

[F5] **Weak derivatives of spatial products.** For $u,v\in H^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C)$ the product $u(x)v(y)$ has weak derivatives $D_x^\alpha D_y^\beta(u(x)v(y))=(D^\alpha u)(x)(D^\beta v)(y)$ for $|\alpha|+|\beta|\le2$, obtained by iterated weak-derivative testing and Fubini. Their squared $L^2(\mathbb R^6)$ norms are $\|D^\alpha u\|_2^2\|D^\beta v\|_2^2<\infty$, including mixed first derivatives. Thus the spatial products and $f_\pm$ lie in $H^2(\mathbb R^6)$, without claiming an exact unproved Sobolev norm constant ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]). On these products the unbounded differential slot action is $(-a\Delta_x-a\Delta_y+V_b)(u(x)v(y))=(hu)(x)v(y)+u(x)(hv)(y)$; every term lies in $L^2$ by its factor norms. This is an exact-domain calculation, not an application of bounded tensor-map rules to an unbounded $h$.

[F6] **Finite means of domain preparations.** For a unit vector $\psi$ in the domain of a self-adjoint assigned $A$, the absolute first spectral moment is finite and its mean is $\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[pthm-nrqm-observables-preparation-moments]] clause (a), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct; transport the spatial/spin products into the actual declared tensor square, verify their full-domain slot actions, and evaluate the real direct/exchange means.

**Given:** The data of the statement and [F1]–[F6].

1.1 [Unit preparations in the actual combined sector] Orthonormality of $u,v$ makes $u\otimes v$ and $v\otimes u$ orthogonal unit vectors, so $\varphi_\pm$ and $f_\pm$ are unit and satisfy $f_\pm(y,x)=\pm f_\pm(x,y)$. The displayed spin definitions give $\|\chi_\pm\|=1$ and $R\chi_\pm=\pm\chi_\pm$. Hence $\mathcal U(f_\pm\chi_\mp)(x,y)=R f_\pm(y,x)\chi_\mp=-f_\pm(x,y)\chi_\mp$. Their $L^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$ norm is one. By [F1], $\Phi_\pm=\Theta_2^{-1}(f_\pm\chi_\mp)$ are unit vectors in the declared $\mathfrak H_2^-$, so their pure projectors define the declared preparations. This proves (a). [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 [H² domain and exact one-body expectation] By [F5], each spatial product is in $H^2(\mathbb R^6)$, hence so is $f_\pm$. Multiplication by the fixed finite spin vector means a finite tuple of constant scalar multiples of $f_\pm$, so $f_\pm\chi_\mp\in H^2(\mathbb R^6;\mathbb C^4)$. Step 1.1 and [F4] then place $\Phi_\pm$ in the exact domain of $H_2^-$. Write $q(x,y)=u(x)v(y)$, $r(x,y)=v(x)u(y)$ and $L=-a\Delta_x-a\Delta_y+V_b$. By [F5], $Lq=(hu)(x)v(y)+u(x)(hv)(y)$ and $Lr=(hv)(x)u(y)+v(x)(hu)(y)$. Fubini gives $\langle Lq,q\rangle=\langle Lr,r\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$, and $\langle Lq,r\rangle=\langle hu,v\rangle\langle v,u\rangle+\langle u,v\rangle\langle hv,u\rangle=0$; the reversed cross pairing vanishes in the same way. Thus $\langle Lf_\pm,f_\pm\rangle=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v$. Spin independence and $\|\chi_\mp\|=1$ give the same pairing in the full spin representation. The unbounded slot terms all had their stated domain inputs. [step 1.1, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

3.1 [Pair expectation and reality] In the bounded case, absolute values of $D$ and $X$ are bounded by $\|W\|_\infty\|u\|_2^2\|v\|_2^2$; the crossed term uses $\int|uv|\le\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$. In the Coulomb case $H^2\subset H^1$, so [F3] gives absolute convergence and $f_\pm\in D(M_W)$. For either real even kernel, exchanging $x,y$ in the absolutely convergent $X$ integral gives $X=\overline X$; the two direct diagonal terms are equal to $D$. Expanding $|f_\pm|^2$ therefore gives $\langle M_Wf_\pm,f_\pm\rangle=D\pm X$, as in [F3]. The full spin-independent pair multiplier has exactly this expectation in $f_\pm\chi_\mp$. No orbitals were required to be real. [step 2.1, F1, F2, F3, algebra]

4.1 [Finite energy means and splitting] By step 2.1 the vectors lie in the self-adjoint sector energy domain of [F4], so [F6] guarantees finite energy means. The unitary $\Theta_2$ preserves the energy pairings. Combining the one-body result of step 2.1 and pair result of step 3.1 gives $m_{\rho_\pm}(H_2^-)=\varepsilon_u+\varepsilon_v+D\pm X$. Subtracting proves $m_{\rho_+}-m_{\rho_-}=2X$. This proves (b) on the full stated bounded or Coulomb model, including the original bounded external potential. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F1, F4, F6, algebra]

5.1 [Repulsive ordering and scope] In the repulsive Coulomb case [F3] gives $X\ge0$ under the original complex $H^1$ hypothesis, which is already satisfied by the stated $H^2$ orbitals. Step 4.1 therefore gives $m_{\rho_-}(H_2^-)\le m_{\rho_+}(H_2^-)$, proving (c). The $H^1$ interaction inequality does not alone assert an energy mean for vectors outside the energy domain. Step 1.1 supplies the actual adopted fermion sector, and every energy compared in step 4.1 is a finite mean of the declared preparation; no atomic-state approximation, measured splitting or derived spin-statistics rule was used. This proves (d) and completes the statement. [step 1.1, step 4.1, F3, F4, F6, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

- **What the exchange term is.** $X$ is the integral of the overlap density $\overline uv$ against its translate; it is not an interaction between distinguishable particles, and its sign in the repulsive-Coulomb case is the content of clause (c). The theorem compares two declared preparations of the same model; it does not claim that a many-electron ground state is either of them.
- **Bounded versus Coulomb.** The bounded case relies on the elementary expectation identity of the math supplier and requires only $u,v\in W^{2,2}$; the Coulomb case additionally uses the Hardy-type bound of that supplier to make $D$ and $X$ finite and to obtain $X\ge0$.
